item.title: Manchester City 1 Aston Villa 2 : A common issue resurfaces for City at Villa Park
item.description: Manchester City 1 Aston Villa 2 : A common issue resurfaces for City at Villa Park Manchester City 1 (Erling Haaland 52′) Aston Villa 2 (Nicolas Jackson 6′, 60) Manchester City’s seven-match winning run in the Premier League came to an end today as they went down to a 2-1 defeat to Aston Villa at Villa Park. Nicolas Jackson bagged a brace for Unai Emery’s side and Erling Haaland scored City’s goals. Errors from Marc Guehi and Gianluigi Donnarumma proved costly and individual errors are becoming a theme of Manchester City’s play at the back. When the starting lineups were announced Enzo Maresca made four changes to the starting lineup that beat AEK Athens. Erling Haaland, Marc Guehi, Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye came in for Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Allan and Floyd Samba. Mateo Kovacic and Nico O’Reilly returned to the bench while Matheus Nunes was not included in Manchester City’s matchday squad for today’s match. First half. Aston Villa burst out of the traps to begin the game. They were well and truly up for the game and enjoyed the majority of possession in the opening five minutes. Gianluigi Donnarumma conceded a corner for delaying a goal kick, which summed up the start that Enzo Maresca’s side had made to the match. Nicolas Jackson gives Aston Villa a deserved lead as Marc Guehi once again costs his team. Aston Villa would take a deserved lead in the sixth minute. Marc Guehi was played a ball on the left-hand side of City’s defence but his frankly horrible first touch gave away possession to Nicolas Jackson who was through on goal. Jackson surged into a great position in the City area and showed great composure and produced a thundering finish from close range that rifled into the roof of the net to give Unai Emery’s side a deserved lead. That was the third straight goal that a Guehi error had led to a goal, and it is becoming a concern for Manchester City. Iliman Ndiaye forced Aston Villa keeper Zion Suzuki into his first save of the match in the 13th minute. Ndiaye cut inside from the right wing and showed great footwork to leave Villa left-back Ian Maatsen stranded before he fired a low, curling left-footed shot on goal from the edge of the Villa area. Ndiaye’s shot was destined for the bottom corner before Suzuki made a fantastic save at full stretch to his right. Rayan Cherki forced Suzuki into another strong save in the 21st minute. Manchester City played the ball from left to right to get the ball to Doku on the left. Doku drove into the penalty area and cut the ball inside to Rayan Cherki. Cherki got a strong shot on target from 10 yards out which Suzuki got down well to save to his right. Cherki’s shot had the power but it was too close to the Aston Villa keeper. item.content:encoded: Manchester City 1 Aston Villa 2 : A common issue resurfaces for City at Villa Park Manchester City 1 (Erling Haaland 52′) Aston Villa 2 (Nicolas Jackson 6′, 60) Manchester City’s seven-match winning run in the Premier League came to an end today as they went down to a 2-1 defeat to Aston Villa at Villa Park. Nicolas Jackson bagged a brace for Unai Emery’s side and Erling Haaland scored City’s goals. Errors from Marc Guehi and Gianluigi Donnarumma proved costly and individual errors are becoming a theme of Manchester City’s play at the back. When the starting lineups were announced Enzo Maresca made four changes to the starting lineup that beat AEK Athens. Erling Haaland, Marc Guehi, Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye came in for Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Allan and Floyd Samba. Mateo Kovacic and Nico O’Reilly returned to the bench while Matheus Nunes was not included in Manchester City’s matchday squad for today’s match. First half. Aston Villa burst out of the traps to begin the game. They were well and truly up for the game and enjoyed the majority of possession in the opening five minutes. Gianluigi Donnarumma conceded a corner for delaying a goal kick, which summed up the start that Enzo Maresca’s side had made to the match. Nicolas Jackson gives Aston Villa a deserved lead as Marc Guehi once again costs his team. Aston Villa would take a deserved lead in the sixth minute. Marc Guehi was played a ball on the left-hand side of City’s defence but his frankly horrible first touch gave away possession to Nicolas Jackson who was through on goal. Jackson surged into a great position in the City area and showed great composure and produced a thundering finish from close range that rifled into the roof of the net to give Unai Emery’s side a deserved lead. That was the third straight goal that a Guehi error had led to a goal, and it is becoming a concern for Manchester City. Iliman Ndiaye forced Aston Villa keeper Zion Suzuki into his first save of the match in the 13th minute. Ndiaye cut inside from the right wing and showed great footwork to leave Villa left-back Ian Maatsen stranded before he fired a low, curling left-footed shot on goal from the edge of the Villa area. Ndiaye’s shot was destined for the bottom corner before Suzuki made a fantastic save at full stretch to his right. Rayan Cherki forced Suzuki into another strong save in the 21st minute. Manchester City played the ball from left to right to get the ball to Doku on the left. Doku drove into the penalty area and cut the ball inside to Rayan Cherki. Cherki got a strong shot on target from 10 yards out which Suzuki got down well to save to his right. Cherki’s shot had the power but it was too close to the Aston Villa keeper. However, Enzo Maresca’s side had grown into the game and were on top following Aston Villa’s fast start. City begin to pile on the pressure as Khusanov forces another save from Zion Suzuki. Abdukodir Khusanov would be the next City player to force Zion Suzuki into a save. City again dropped Villa deep into their own area. Jeremy Doku again played a ball from the left into a dangerous position that the Villa defence initially cleared. The ball was worked to Khusanov who fired a low shot from 25 yards out on the right that Suzuki got down well to save. Iliman Ndiaye hit the post in the 28th minute. Manchester City played through the Villa pass and Rayan Cherki was found in space in the middle of the pitch. Cherki drove forward and played the ball out wide to Iliman Ndiaye. Ndiaye drove at Ian Maatsen and curled another low effort across Zion Suzuki to the far post from the right. Ndiaye’s shot beat the Villa keeper but hit the post and went wide. Approaching the 40th minute, Aston Villa were defending well and posing City their own threat. Particularly with the long ball over the top of City’s defence aimed towards Nicolas Jackson. Also, Manchester City were having trouble at times playing out from the back, especially from goal kicks. In the 40th minute, Ruben Dias would make a goal saving challenge to block Aston Villa winger Alysson’s left-footed shot from close range after the Brazilian winger surged into the City area after a great run inside from the right wing. Both teams would have moments before the halftime whistle blew. Aston Villa would take a 1-0 lead into the interval after they were rewarded for their fast start to the match. Thoughts and observations from Manchester City’s first half performance. After Aston Villa burst out of the traps to begin the game, Manchester City did dominate large portions of the first half. Only the post and Aston Villa keeper Zion Suzuki prevented Enzo Maresca’s side from finding an equalizer. However, there were areas of concern for Enzo Maresca to address at halftime. A major one Ruben Dias was getting drawn out of position in the heart of City’s defence by clever movement from John McGinn. McGinn would start up front then drift into midfield. This was drawing the Manchester City captain out and leaving a big hole for Nicolas Jackson to operate in. That did seem to be Villa’s path to a second goal. However, it wasn’t all doom and gloom for City. Far from it. They did play well after Villa’s fast start and the game was well and truly alive at halftime. Second half. Enzo Maresca brought on Rico Lewis and Phil Foden for Marc Guehi at halftime. Abdukodir Khusanov moved to centre-back with Lewis slotting in at right-back. Lewis gave away possession to begin the second half, which led to a Villa counterattack that was defended well by City at the cost of a corner. Aston Villa’s corner came to nothing, but it was an early warning for Enzo Maresca’s side after the interval. Erling Haaland heads home to give Manchester City the equalizer they deserved. Manchester City would get a well-deserved equalizer in the 52nd minute. Iliman Ndiaye was fouled by Boubacar Kamara around 30 yards from goal after some great City pressing won back possession high up the pitch. It did seem like Enzo Fernandez would take the opportunity to get an attempt on goal. Instead, he played the ball to the right wing to Iliman Ndiaye. Ndiaye stood up Ian Maatsen and played a great cross into a dangerous area. Erling Haaland towered over the Villa defence to head home from close to make it 1-1. It was a great set piece routine from City which caught out the Aston Villa defence. Zion Suzuki would deny a thunderous Josko Gvardiol shot from close range to keep the score at 1-1 in the 56th minute. Jeremy Doku had Aston Villa right-back Matty Cash right where he wanted him after Cash picked up a yellow card a minute earlier. Cash stood off Doku which allowed the Belgian winger time to pick out Josko Gvardiol in the Villa area after the Croatian international made a great run into the box. Gvardiol unleashed a stinging shot on goal from the left-hand side of the penalty spot that Suzuki tipped over the crossbar. Nicolas Jackson restores Aston Villa’s lead after a sweeping Villa counter. Aston Villa would retake the lead in the 60th minute. A long ball was played up towards Nicolas Jackson who won his aerial duel and the ball was played out wide to Ibrahim Mbaye. Mbaye had acres of space to operate in and he played a great ball to Jackson who was unmarked just inside the City area. Jackson’s shot had power and squirmed in as Gianluigi Donnarumma dove over the top of the ball while trying to make a routine save. It was a poor goal for City to concede. Donnarumma should have done a lot better with Jackson’s shot. Manchester City almost had another equaliser in the 67th minute. Jeremy Doku got himself into a great position to cross on the left and the ball came across the Villa area. It was poorly cleared by the Aston Villa defence ans the ball squirmed to Josko Gvardiol. Gvardiol got a shot away from close range but Zion Suzuki reacted quickly to the danger to smother Gvardiol’s shot. The game had become disjointed as it ticked into the 77th minute. There was a

item.title: 16yo Arsenal summer signing scores 3 in 3 games
item.description: 16yo Arsenal summer signing scores 3 in 3 games Mylo Bernard continued his strong early Arsenal form with another goal for the u18s on Saturday, as they eased past Aston Villa for three points. Photo via Arsenal.com Arsenal summer signing Mylo Bernard made his mark in his first start for the u18s last week, scoring a brace as the young Gunners came from behind to beat Tottenham Hotspur 2-1. Bernard was named in the starting lineup against this weekend, and he played a part in a lightning fast start for Arsenal against Aston Villa . Team captain Teshaun Murisa gave Arsenal the lead in the 7th minute, winning the ball on the edge of the area before converting for 1-0. Then fellow summer signing Axel Donczew scored in the 11th minute to double the team’s lead. Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images Arsenal really looked like running away with the game by the time Bernard scored in the 16th minute, beating the goalkeeper one-on-one after a through ball by Daniel McCarron . But it was Villa who scored next, with Jake Doughty pulling one back in the 21st minute for 3-1. Fortunately, Arsenal remained in control, and the Gunners were more likely to add to their lead than give it up in the second half. Murisa, Donczew, and Bernard all had chances to add to their first-half goals, but a miss and two good saves ensured the scoreline didn’t change. Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images Bernard now has three goals in three u18 Premier League matches with Arsenal, whilst Donczew has two goals and an assist in four. Arsenal also signed Vincent Joseph from Liverpool over the summer, and the 16-year-old came on for his debut in the last half-hour against Villa. All in all, it’s looking like the academy made some smart moves in the summer market, and they’re reaping the rewards now. Arsenal u18 lineup vs Aston Villa Phillips, Owusu-Gyasi, Abubakar, McCarron, Mbala, Purdy, Munoz, Murisa, Bernard, Nwaneri, Donczew Substitutes Joseph (for Nwaneri, 63), Odaji-Ukueku (for Murisa, 77), Bonaventure Yetna (for Bernard, 90), Lupinski, Stachow, Oba, Raymond-Callender Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images

item.title: There’s only one man who can help United and the club’s NOT seriously considering him – Opinion
item.description: There’s only one man who can help United and the club’s NOT seriously considering him – Opinion Manchester United are back in a position that fans were dreading they would be in at this point of the season: considering who should be their next manager. At the time of writing, Carrick is still the boss, and it is entirely possible that something could suddenly swing his way, as unlikely as it seems at the moment. Lots of names have been floated around recently, especially after the heavy and embarrassing loss to Como mid-week, but there is probably only one with the most potential to succeed. Fans are well aware of the toxic atmosphere, the lack of structure and forward planning, and the financial mess in which the club finds itself. Given these elements, it seems that United can only go for a very particular type of manager; otherwise, they are doomed to stay in this vicious cycle. When we think of the criteria needed, a few things spring to mind: we need someone who is able to work on a budget, with a limited and mish-mash of profiles in a squad, is enough of a tactician, and has Premier League experience, preferably at a big club. Out of the names in mainstream media—Fabian Hurzeler, Julian Nagelsmann, and Eddie Howe seem to be the ones most mentioned. Hurzeler would be crazy to leave Brighton, given the structure and momentum he has at Brighton, even if United’s pull and appeal are always huge. Nagelsmann is a bright and young tactician who would need the club to be set up in a pretty specific way for him to succeed, and even then, there are minor question marks over how his teams seem to get counter-attacked. His time at the helm of the German national team has not really done his reputation many favours, even if international football is a different ball game. Howe is brilliant at setting his teams up out of possession, but his time at Newcastle was marked by a consistent inability to break down stubborn teams in possession—a task that would be needed at United. None of these names seem the perfect fit, nor do they inspire a great deal of confidence, at least for this writer. Unai Emery has been mentioned in passing, and in my opinion, he would be the best bet. In an ideal world, fans would be able to trust in the club’s structure and setup, but it is clear nothing is going to change and INEOS are pretty much the same as the Glazers, with Jason Wilcox basically being the equivalent of Ed Woodward. Emery has a track record of dealing with all sorts of players and profiles and is able to make his teams look better than the sum of their parts. This is invaluable and perfect for United, who seem completely incapable of squad building well enough to actually have a group of players with similar qualities, which is obviously a result of the constant manager changes. item.content:encoded: There’s only one man who can help United and the club’s NOT seriously considering him – Opinion Manchester United are back in a position that fans were dreading they would be in at this point of the season: considering who should be their next manager. At the time of writing, Carrick is still the boss, and it is entirely possible that something could suddenly swing his way, as unlikely as it seems at the moment. Lots of names have been floated around recently, especially after the heavy and embarrassing loss to Como mid-week, but there is probably only one with the most potential to succeed. Fans are well aware of the toxic atmosphere, the lack of structure and forward planning, and the financial mess in which the club finds itself. Given these elements, it seems that United can only go for a very particular type of manager; otherwise, they are doomed to stay in this vicious cycle. When we think of the criteria needed, a few things spring to mind: we need someone who is able to work on a budget, with a limited and mish-mash of profiles in a squad, is enough of a tactician, and has Premier League experience, preferably at a big club. Out of the names in mainstream media—Fabian Hurzeler, Julian Nagelsmann, and Eddie Howe seem to be the ones most mentioned. Hurzeler would be crazy to leave Brighton, given the structure and momentum he has at Brighton, even if United’s pull and appeal are always huge. Nagelsmann is a bright and young tactician who would need the club to be set up in a pretty specific way for him to succeed, and even then, there are minor question marks over how his teams seem to get counter-attacked. His time at the helm of the German national team has not really done his reputation many favours, even if international football is a different ball game. Howe is brilliant at setting his teams up out of possession, but his time at Newcastle was marked by a consistent inability to break down stubborn teams in possession—a task that would be needed at United. None of these names seem the perfect fit, nor do they inspire a great deal of confidence, at least for this writer. Unai Emery has been mentioned in passing, and in my opinion, he would be the best bet. In an ideal world, fans would be able to trust in the club’s structure and setup, but it is clear nothing is going to change and INEOS are pretty much the same as the Glazers, with Jason Wilcox basically being the equivalent of Ed Woodward. Emery has a track record of dealing with all sorts of players and profiles and is able to make his teams look better than the sum of their parts. This is invaluable and perfect for United, who seem completely incapable of squad building well enough to actually have a group of players with similar qualities, which is obviously a result of the constant manager changes. Emery has gone through many squad overhauls at Aston Villa and constantly has them performing at a decent level, for many years now. He is respected as a tactician, and his time at Villarreal also showed he is able to work with a shoestring budget and still deliver. The Spaniard also has big club experience at Arsenal, and while that did not end well, it is not hard to imagine how he would have performed with the champions with the current squad. As good a job as Mikel Arteta has done, Emery did not have the luxuries he does, and likely would have won the league too if he had been backed in this same way with the same quality of players. His negative experience with the Gunners might even be a positive in the sense that he has been through the highly pressured environment of a big club underperforming. The reason Emery is reportedly not on the shortlist for United seems to be financially related, as it would take quite the fee to release him from Villa. However, that is a crazy reason for a club like Manchester United not to consider a manager. Fans were told the club were waiting it out for Dan Ashworth as he is THE man and there is no point pursuing any other director of football. Obviously, that blew up in their face anyway, but putting that aside, if the right person is there, you have to do all you can to bring them in, and finances should not be the issue. After all, what is the point of going with another, potentially less capable or less suitable manager who might struggle to get the club to qualify for next season’s Champions League. The financial loss of missing out would likely outweigh the cost of just shelling out for Emery or whoever those in charge feel is the best fit. It is not surprising Wilcox’s shortlist includes two of three managers who can be hired for free. It is hard to feel like much will change with that current shortlist, and we would be doomed to ruin another manager’s future, just as with Ruben Amorim , who also needed a very particular setup to succeed.

item.title: Jerry Jones Backs Cowboys’ Coaching Structure as Brian Schottenheimer Faces Pressure
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys are facing mounting pressure after a disappointing start to the 2026 season; however, owner Jerry Jones is not ready to sound the alarm. Despite growing criticism of head coach Brian Schottenheimer and the coaching staff, the owner believes the organization has the structure and personnel needed to turn things around. The Cowboys sit at 2-4 following a 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 6. With questions emerging about the team’s coaching decisions, defensive struggles, and disappointing results, Jones has offered a firm vote of confidence in the staff as the Cowboys look to get their season back on track. Jerry Jones Expresses Confidence In Brian Schottenheimer And The Cowboys’ Coaching Staff Oct 18, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones looks looks on prior to the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Jones recently addressed the Cowboys’ situation during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan, pushing back against concerns about the team’s coaching structure. The Cowboys owner believes the staff is positioned to identify its shortcomings and make the necessary adjustments. Jones said while discussing the head coach and the coaching staff, according to Cowboys reporter Jon Machota. “We’re in good shape,” “I’m very confident. … We have every reason to believe we’ll make the right adjustments.” Cowboys owner Jerry Jones on @1053thefan while talking about Brian Schottenheimer and Dallas' coaching staff: "We're in good shape." Jones said they're structured well throughout their staff to fix their current issues. "I'm very confident. … We have every reason to believe… — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) October 23, 2026 His comments come amid increasing scrutiny of Schottenheimer, who is in his second season as the Cowboys’ HC. Their 2-4 record has intensified questions about whether the current coaching setup can deliver better results, particularly as the defense struggles to contain opposing offenses. The criticism has also extended to Jones’ approach to coaching salaries. NFL insider Josina Anderson suggested that Cowboys ownership wanted to keep Schottenheimer and his coordinators at league-average salaries for their respective positions. Critics have questioned whether the Cowboys have invested enough in experienced coaching leadership despite its willingness to spend on high-profile players. Schottenheimer’s offensive group features quarterback Dak Prescott and wide receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens; still, the Cowboys have struggled to produce consistent results. Their running game has also been a concern, while defensive coordinator Christian Parker faces the challenge of establishing a dependable unit in his first season leading a defense. item.title: “Total Robbery”: $365 Ticket Hike Adds Another Blow for Dolphins Fans After Winless Season Start
item.description: Supporting an NFL team takes more than time on Sundays. Fans spend money on tickets and travel, and they trust the franchise to give them something worth following. That commitment becomes harder to defend when the losses keep piling up. A rebuilding team like the Miami Dolphins can ask for patience, but that patience has limits. Dolphins Raise Ticket Prices After 0-5 Start The Dolphins are raising all season-ticket prices for the 2027 season after opening their 2026 campaign with five straight losses. Most tickets will rise by 3%, while some shaded seats along the home sideline will see larger increases, according to reports on the renewal notices sent to members. Oct 4, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Vikings fans cheer before the game against the Miami Dolphins at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reported on X that the Dolphins kept prices unchanged or lowered them for the 2026 season, then raised them across the board for 2027. The reason is an additional regular-season home game next year. The Dolphins, who lowered or kept prices the same for all season tickets this season, are raising all season ticket prices for next season, to account for an extra regular season home game in 2027. (Total number of home games remains 10, including preseason, but 9 will be regular season next year). Price increase is 3 % for most. A couple sections in shade on home sideline rose a bit more than 3%. Renewals went out today. — Barry Jackson (@flasportsbuzz) October 21, 2026 The total remains 10 home games, including preseason. The package will include nine regular-season games and one preseason game instead of eight regular-season games and two preseason games. That scheduling change gives Miami a clear reason to charge more. A regular-season game generally carries more value than a preseason contest, so the increase does not mean fans are paying more for an identical package. Still, the timing is difficult for a team that has yet to win a game and is already working through a major roster rebuild. Dolphins Fans Face Higher Costs While Results Remain Poor The impact will be greater for some season-ticket holders than the 3% figure suggests. Dan Muchnick, a ticket holder since the franchise’s inaugural 1966 season, saw the price of each shaded seat in Section 144 climb from $3,430 to $3,795. That is a $365 increase per seat, or about 10.6%, according to reporting by The Miami Herald . Sep 20, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; A Miami Dolphins fan reacts during the second half of the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi’s Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Attendance gives the Dolphins another reason to pay attention to the value fans receive. Miami averaged 58,719 spectators across its first two home games, ranking 31st in the NFL at the time of the report. Mandatory Credit: Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reported on X that the Dolphins kept prices unchanged or lowered them for the 2026 season, then raised them across the board for 2027. The reason is an additional regular-season home game next year. The Dolphins, who lowered or kept prices the same for all season tickets this season, are raising all season ticket prices for next season, to account for an extra regular season home game in 2027. (Total number of home games remains 10, including preseason, but 9 will be regular season next year). Price increase is 3 % for most. A couple sections in shade on home sideline rose a bit more than 3%. Renewals went out today. — Barry Jackson (@flasportsbuzz) October 21, 2026 The total remains 10 home games, including preseason. The package will include nine regular-season games and one preseason game instead of eight regular-season games and two preseason games. That scheduling change gives Miami a clear reason to charge more. A regular-season game generally carries more value than a preseason contest, so the increase does not mean fans are paying more for an identical package. Still, the timing is difficult for a team that has yet to win a game and is already working through a major roster rebuild. Dolphins Fans Face Higher Costs While Results Remain Poor The impact will be greater for some season-ticket holders than the 3% figure suggests. Dan Muchnick, a ticket holder since the franchise’s inaugural 1966 season, saw the price of each shaded seat in Section 144 climb from $3,430 to $3,795. That is a $365 increase per seat, or about 10.6%, according to reporting by The Miami Herald . Sep 20, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; A Miami Dolphins fan reacts during the second half of the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi’s Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Attendance gives the Dolphins another reason to pay attention to the value fans receive. Miami averaged 58,719 spectators across its first two home games, ranking 31st in the NFL at the time of the report. The team averaged 65,687 across eight home games at Hard Rock Stadium in 2025, before its ninth home game was played in Madrid. There is a reasonable argument for adjusting prices when the season-ticket package includes another regular-season game. Miami also held or reduced prices for the current season, rather than raising them immediately after the previous campaign. It is not completely true that the team is raising prices without giving fans anything back. Still, the Dolphins are asking fans for more money even though they have not won any games yet and the team is still struggling to get better. An extra game increases the price. But fans are mad about how the team plays. Miami needs to show that the games are worth the money. If the team plays better, the price hike will make more sense. item.title: Is Stephen A. Smith Right to Defend Lamar Jackson Amid Growing Criticism?
item.description: Stephen A. Smith is standing up for quarterback Lamar Jackson as criticism surrounding the Baltimore Ravens quarterback continues to grow. With Jackson dealing with an ankle injury and uncertainty surrounding his availability for the team’s Week 7 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals, questions about his health and the Ravens’ struggles have become a major talking point; however, Smith believes the criticism should not overshadow what Jackson has accomplished throughout his NFL career. The ESPN analyst addressed the debate on First Take, pushing back against the idea that Jackson should be judged differently because of his recent injury concerns. His message was clear: Jackson’s current situation should not lead people to forget the quarterback he has consistently proven himself to be. Stephen A. Smith Pushes Back Against Criticism Of Lamar Jackson Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) runs in a QB keeper for a touchdown in the first quarter of the NFL Week 6 game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Cincinnati Bengals at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore on Sunday, Oct. 13, 2019. Cincinnati Bengals At Baltimore Ravens Smith made his position clear while di scussing the criticism directed at the Ravens QB, urging people not to confuse injury concerns with a decline in ability. “You defend Lamar Jackson the way you’ve always tried to defend him. … Don’t assume he ain’t what he used to be.” “You defend Lamar Jackson the way you’ve always tried to defend him. … Don’t assume he ain’t what he used to be.” @stephenasmith weighs in on defending Lamar Jackson pic.twitter.com/2JeOhb3IrL — First Take (@FirstTake) October 23, 2026 Jackson has missed the Ravens’ last two games after suffering a left ankle injury. His absence has exposed how heavily the Ravens rely on his unique ability to threaten defenses as both a passer and a runner. Backup quarterback Tyler Huntley has stepped in; however, the Ravens’ offense has struggled to maintain the same explosiveness without its two-time NFL MVP. The star QB’s mobility is a major part of what makes the Ravens dangerous. Defenses should be aware that he will retain the football and rush, giving more chances for his running back, Derrick Henry, to carry the ball. This would not be possible without such an option; therefore, defenses would put more pressure on Derrick Henry and force Baltimore to find other ways to advance their game. item.title: ESPN predicts the final score of Wisconsin football vs. USC in Week 8
item.description: The Wisconsin Badgers have a chance to virtually guarantee themselves bowl eligibility this weekend against the No. 15 USC Trojans . With a win, Luke Fickell’s side will be pushed to 5-2, with the season’s most challenging games largely out of the way. However, standing in the way of a 5-2 record is one of the nation’s most prolific offenses who average 462.4 yards per game. The Trojans are 6-1, with one loss coming against the Oregon Ducks in a high-scoring 41-27 affair. ESPN's Bill Connelly’s SP+ metric is one of the most widely accepted measures in all of college football, and unfortunately for Wisconsin fans, the Badgers are projected to lose 28-23. What will be the deciding factor? The biggest storyline going into this will be one of the nation’s best offenses (USC) vs. one of the best defenses (Wisconsin). While each team will have its fair share of plays to cancel one another out on that side, this will be a game that will be decided by whether Wisconsin’s offense can put together its best performance of the season. With the Badgers averaging just 341 yards per game, until they prove otherwise, there is little reason to think this offense will turn things around this weekend. Connelly's full prediction USC's projected margin of victory : 4.5 points Wisconsin's win probability : 39% Final score : USC 28, Wisconsin 23 Spread : USC -2.5 Contact/Follow @TheBadgersWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Wisconsin Badgers news, notes and opinion. This article originally appeared on Badgers Wire: ESPN predicts the final score of Wisconsin football vs. USC in Week 8

item.title: WWE Legend Ric Flair Hospitalized After Falling Outside Restaurant, While ‘Dealing’ with Blood Clot in His Leg
item.description: Ric Flair at the 44th Annual Sports Emmy Awards in New York City on May, 22, 2023 Credit: Arturo Holmes/Getty NEED TO KNOW Ric Flair was reportedly treated by medical staff after falling outside a Tampa restaurant on Friday, Oct. 23 His daughter Charlotte Flair said in a social media post that the WWE legend is “going to be ok” Flair, 77, had canceled a Seattle appearance hours before the fall as doctors limited his travel due to a blood clot in his leg Ric Flair is recovering in the hospital after a fall outside a restaurant in Florida. The retired WWE legend, 77, was injured in a fall outside Wagamama in Tampa on Friday, Oct. 23, TMZ reported. The incident occurred hours after Flair revealed on Instagram that an upcoming appearance was being canceled due to a blood clot in his leg. In photos obtained by TMZ, Flair is seen lying on his back while surrounded by medical staff. He is also pictured being transported into an ambulance. Flair left his phone and drink behind as he walked across the street after visiting the restaurant that morning, per the outlet. He reportedly cut his head in the fall and his eye was “bleeding extensively.” Ric Flair at the Staples Center on October 04, 2019 Credit: Jerod Harris/Getty Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! Flair’s daughter, WWE wrestler Charlotte Flair , shared an update on his condition in a post on X on Saturday, Oct. 24. “Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head … (ps: he’s going to be ok),” she wrote. The wrestling legend had shared a lengthy post about his health, hours before he fell. “I want to sincerely apologize to my agent, Steve Solomon … and especially all my fans in Seattle for having to cancel my scheduled appearance,” said Flair. “Unfortunately, I am dealing with a blood clot in my leg, and my doctors have limited my travel to 3–4 hours. Seattle falls outside that range, and as disappointed as I am, I have to put my health and recovery first.” “Blood clots are extremely serious and can be life-threatening. We have seen this recently with Jalen Hurts and the complications involving blood clots in his lungs,” he continued. “It is a reminder that this is not something to take lightly, and I must follow medical advice.” Ric Flair in February 1992 Credit: Steve Taylor/WWE via Getty Flair said that he is scheduled to undergo a procedure “to strip the affected vein,” which will hopefully allow him to travel more and continue with his work commitments. “Please know this decision was not made lightly. I am truly sorry for the inconvenience and disappointment, and I am incredibly grateful for your patience, understanding, and continued support,” he concluded. Flair has had numerous health issues throughout the years. item.title: Frederick Richard wins gymnastics world title on floor exercise after gold-medal guarantee
item.description: On May 5, Frederick Richard guaranteed that he would win a gold medal at the World Gymnastics Championships in five months' time. Richard delivered in his final routine of worlds on Saturday, claiming his first title on floor exercise in Rotterdam, Netherlands. "I hope this is a lesson to everybody that you don't have to wait to get the win to say you will be a champion," Richard said. "You don't have to know when it's going to happen or how it's going to happen, but believing it every second of every day does pay off. I'm proof of that now." Richard, a 22-year-old University of Michigan graduate, tallied 14.633 points, edging Brit Jake Jarman, the 2025 World champion, by 33 thousandths of a point. He won over a field that included the last two Olympic gold medalists. GYMNASTICS WORLDS: Results | Broadcast Schedule Richard added his first global title to his bronze medals from the all-around at the 2023 Worlds and from the team event at the 2024 Paris Olympics. He's the first American man to win a world title on floor since 2003, when Paul Hamm shared gold. He's also the first American man to win a global championship medal in team, all-around and individual apparatus finals since Danell Leyva, who bagged eight career medals between the Olympics and worlds from 2011 through 2016. Frederick Richard turns to Google Doc to plan for LA 2028 Olympics, and to remember Paris 2024 Frederick Richard eyes his first national all-around title at the Xfinity U.S. Gymnastics Championships this week, live on Peacock and NBCSN. Nick Zaccardi , Also Saturday, Americans Claire Pease and Skye Blakely took silver and bronze on vault behind Brazilian Rebeca Andrade, who claimed her third world title in the event. Pease, 17, earned her first individual medal in her first World Championships. Blakely, 21, completed a set of medals in Rotterdam after being part of the silver-medal team and winning all-around gold on Friday. The World Championships conclude Sunday with the last set of apparatus finals — women's beam and floor and men's vault, parallel bars and high bar — live on Peacock at 9 a.m. ET. Skye Blakely wins gymnastics world all-around title, capping a tearful comeback The World Gymnastics Championships continue Saturday with the first of two days of apparatus finals, live on Peacock and NBCSN. Nick Zaccardi ,

item.title: Why Cadillac F1 boss provoked fresh intrigue by dodging driver question
item.description: Motorsport photo The US GP weekend naturally means the spotlight gravitates towards Formula 1’s two American-owned teams. That has led to some awkward questions for Cadillac amid ongoing speculation over its driver line-up for 2027 and beyond. Both Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas are on “multi-year” contracts, understood to be a so-called one-plus-one arrangement in which the second year is optional, subject to either party fulfilling various conditions. Such has been the disparity in performance between the two drivers that Bottas’s position has been the object of paddock gossip for months. Recently appointed team principal Marcin Budkowski has already had to do some firefighting on this, as had his predecessor Graeme Lowdon. But a rather peculiar moment in the FIA’s press conference for team representatives on Friday in Austin suggested Cadillac’s plans aren’t as fixed as previously billed. The catalyst was a soft question from one of the broadcasters on the theme of Perez’s upcoming 300th grand prix start: “How difficult is it to evaluate a driver who’s fighting at the back of the grid, at the same time as the impression is that he’s having a better season than his team-mate? And quickly on drivers, would you be interested in having any conversation with Esteban [Ocon] regarding maybe a reserve role?” In trying to give a suitably anodyne non-answer, Budkowski began to flounder. “Look, for a driver like Checo, who, as you said, has a huge amount of experience and a number of races, I can tell you he doesn’t behave or drive like a driver who is anywhere close to retirement,” hew said. “He’s pushing very hard behind the wheel. He’s pushing us very hard also behind the scenes, in the debrief rooms and outside, and regularly texting me and other members of the team to push us to improve. He’s hungry, he’s motivated, and that’s actually really good to see. He does it in his own style. Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing “We have two drivers: one is more hot and one is probably more cold, if we could say, from there. And they both push the team in their own particular ways, but Checo is, yes, pushing us very hard. And just looking at the way his body language on the grid, when he gets his helmet on and he gets in the car, he’s getting ready for a fight. There’s a lot of fire, there’s a lot of motivation there, so it’s really impressive for a driver of this experience. “And at the same time, we’re getting his feedback and his input in terms of, as an experienced driver. item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo The US GP weekend naturally means the spotlight gravitates towards Formula 1’s two American-owned teams. That has led to some awkward questions for Cadillac amid ongoing speculation over its driver line-up for 2027 and beyond. Both Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas are on “multi-year” contracts, understood to be a so-called one-plus-one arrangement in which the second year is optional, subject to either party fulfilling various conditions. Such has been the disparity in performance between the two drivers that Bottas’s position has been the object of paddock gossip for months. Recently appointed team principal Marcin Budkowski has already had to do some firefighting on this, as had his predecessor Graeme Lowdon. But a rather peculiar moment in the FIA’s press conference for team representatives on Friday in Austin suggested Cadillac’s plans aren’t as fixed as previously billed. The catalyst was a soft question from one of the broadcasters on the theme of Perez’s upcoming 300th grand prix start: “How difficult is it to evaluate a driver who’s fighting at the back of the grid, at the same time as the impression is that he’s having a better season than his team-mate? And quickly on drivers, would you be interested in having any conversation with Esteban [Ocon] regarding maybe a reserve role?” In trying to give a suitably anodyne non-answer, Budkowski began to flounder. “Look, for a driver like Checo, who, as you said, has a huge amount of experience and a number of races, I can tell you he doesn’t behave or drive like a driver who is anywhere close to retirement,” hew said. “He’s pushing very hard behind the wheel. He’s pushing us very hard also behind the scenes, in the debrief rooms and outside, and regularly texting me and other members of the team to push us to improve. He’s hungry, he’s motivated, and that’s actually really good to see. He does it in his own style. Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing “We have two drivers: one is more hot and one is probably more cold, if we could say, from there. And they both push the team in their own particular ways, but Checo is, yes, pushing us very hard. And just looking at the way his body language on the grid, when he gets his helmet on and he gets in the car, he’s getting ready for a fight. There’s a lot of fire, there’s a lot of motivation there, so it’s really impressive for a driver of this experience. “And at the same time, we’re getting his feedback and his input in terms of, as an experienced driver. So yes, it’s a very good combination. “And sorry, the second question was about Esteban Ocon ? Well, look, as a team principal, and I’m sure it’s the same with my colleagues, you’re getting calls and contacts from every driver or driver manager that is on the market. So, there are a number of drivers and managers who have contacted me. “I’m not going to say who it is or who it isn’t, but pretty much all of them that are on the market have been in touch, as you’d expect. But yes, I think it’s the last place here, as you can imagine, where I would communicate anything on driver line-up.” Were William Shakespeare present, he would no doubt have put quill to parchment and scratched out a note to the effect that the gentleman doth protest too much. Fortunately for the Cadillac team principal, perhaps, Adrian Newey was in the room and acted as a natural magnet for the majority of further questions. Motorsport.com understands that Ocon is highly unlikely to go to Cadillac, since he and Perez mixed like oil and water when they last coexisted under the same roof. It’s believed he will probably become Aston Martin’s third driver. Whether or not Cadillac retain Bottas for 2027, it’s known that the team’s owners wish to have an American driver in a race seat as soon as possible. Lowdon’s surprise replacement this summer is an indication of how General Motors and TWG Motorsports’ expectations appear to be running somewhere ahead of the team’s current progress. Cadillac ran Colton Herta in FP1 at the Circuit of The Americas, but he is a leftfield candidate for any race opportunities since he is one point short of qualifying for a superlicence, owing to the FIA having changed the qualifying rubric. If he has meaningful running in another session this year he will qualify – but his rather patchy Formula 2 campaign this season isn’t a very strong calling card. “Obviously having an American driver in an American team is a great story,” Budkowski told Sky Sports this weekend. “It needs to be the right time and the right driver. But we're working on that. We're working on that with Colton. “There are some really exciting American talents coming up through the ranks as well. We've seen Ugo Ugochukwu winning F3. We've got [Sebastian] Wheldon coming through to F3 next year. “So there's a lot of potential here and we'll look into that obviously.” Read Also: Cadillac reveals date for F1 engine factory debut, thanks drivers for being “patient” Colton Herta “maybe underestimated the difference” from IndyCar – F2 boss To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Chelsea vs. Tottenham Hotspur: game time, live blog, and how to watch online
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur's Mathys Tel (C) is tackled by Chelsea's Estevao (R) during the Sydney Super Cup football match between English Premier League teams Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur at Stadium Australia in Sydney on August 1, 2026. (Photo by Saeed Khan / AFP via Getty Images) / --IMAGE RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE - STRICTLY NO COMMERCIAL USE-- | AFP via Getty Images A glimmer of hope has appeared for Tottenham Hotspur. Some encouraging performances of late have built momentum, culminating in Spurs’ first win of the season following six agonizing winless fixtures. And now we get to ruin all that by paying a visit to Spurs’ proverbial graveyard in the form of Stamford Bridge, as Spurs take on Chelsea. Away matches at Chelsea are never a fun affair, with Spurs having only won once there in 34 attempts. This Chelsea side though are vulnerable, though the relative table positions would say otherwise. item.title: Jose Mourinho talks Yamal, Flick, Camp Nou ahead of Barcelona vs Real Madrid
item.description: Jose Mourinho talks Yamal, Flick, Camp Nou ahead of Barcelona vs Real Madrid Real Madrid have significantly improved their form since their defeat to Atletico Madrid before the start of the September international break. Since that match, the Merengues have been on a roll, winning all of their games against Villarreal, AS Roma, Sevilla, and RB Leipzig . However, they have a significantly more difficult match awaiting them next, as they will travel to Catalonia to face FC Barcelona in the first El Clasico of this season. As MARCA has reported, ahead of this game, Jose Mourinho held his customary press conference and talked about several aspects of the team and the upcoming match. The Portuguese coach believed the form of either of the teams would not matter much in this match: “Good momentum. We’re in good shape and scoring goals. From my experience playing in Clásicos and derbies, what happened before doesn’t mean much.” The Real Madrid coach was ready to take the blame for any failure faced by his team: “I have the feeling that Madrid is just like that. I want nothing more than for my players to receive credit when they do well and for their manager to be criticised when we do less well. That’s the story of every manager. The players win some matches, and the managers lose others. That’s our life. There are at least two Clásicos every season. The most important thing is their global significance. There are other important matches, but this one is unique. The world stops to watch it.” Mourinho was clear that this match will not define the season for the Merengues: “Is this going to be the ultimate test for you? It isn’t. Madrid win trophies with Mourinho.” Ahead of this game, the Portuguese tactician had only good wishes for the referee: “You’ve caught me off guard with that question. The referee’s name never bothers me. I always start from the assumption that the referee is good. What bothers me a little is when the rules are broken. So far, according to the information I’ve received internally, they haven’t been broken. Several referees’ names have been mentioned. Nobody has told me, ‘This is the referee.’ Whoever it is, I wish them well.” The Real Madrid coach did not believe Barcelona’s loss to PSG would affect the Blaugrana team much in the upcoming match: “The defeat in Paris tells me nothing. If we’d lost 4–1 to Leipzig instead of winning 4–1, I’d have been in exactly the same frame of mind for this match.” Mourinho was ready to give the Blaugranes credit for their good start to the season and asked for more patience with his team: “The people who thought a week ago that Barça could thrash us still think the same now. I don’t think that view will change. The fact that people speak highly of Barça doesn’t affect me. To be honest, there are matches in which they obviously deserve plenty of praise because they do some very good things. In our case, we’re viewed as a finished product. Since that match, the Merengues have been on a roll, winning all of their games against Villarreal, AS Roma, Sevilla, and RB Leipzig . However, they have a significantly more difficult match awaiting them next, as they will travel to Catalonia to face FC Barcelona in the first El Clasico of this season. As MARCA has reported, ahead of this game, Jose Mourinho held his customary press conference and talked about several aspects of the team and the upcoming match. The Portuguese coach believed the form of either of the teams would not matter much in this match: “Good momentum. We’re in good shape and scoring goals. From my experience playing in Clásicos and derbies, what happened before doesn’t mean much.” The Real Madrid coach was ready to take the blame for any failure faced by his team: “I have the feeling that Madrid is just like that. I want nothing more than for my players to receive credit when they do well and for their manager to be criticised when we do less well. That’s the story of every manager. The players win some matches, and the managers lose others. That’s our life. There are at least two Clásicos every season. The most important thing is their global significance. There are other important matches, but this one is unique. The world stops to watch it.” Mourinho was clear that this match will not define the season for the Merengues: “Is this going to be the ultimate test for you? It isn’t. Madrid win trophies with Mourinho.” Ahead of this game, the Portuguese tactician had only good wishes for the referee: “You’ve caught me off guard with that question. The referee’s name never bothers me. I always start from the assumption that the referee is good. What bothers me a little is when the rules are broken. So far, according to the information I’ve received internally, they haven’t been broken. Several referees’ names have been mentioned. Nobody has told me, ‘This is the referee.’ Whoever it is, I wish them well.” The Real Madrid coach did not believe Barcelona’s loss to PSG would affect the Blaugrana team much in the upcoming match: “The defeat in Paris tells me nothing. If we’d lost 4–1 to Leipzig instead of winning 4–1, I’d have been in exactly the same frame of mind for this match.” Mourinho was ready to give the Blaugranes credit for their good start to the season and asked for more patience with his team: “The people who thought a week ago that Barça could thrash us still think the same now. I don’t think that view will change. The fact that people speak highly of Barça doesn’t affect me. To be honest, there are matches in which they obviously deserve plenty of praise because they do some very good things. In our case, we’re viewed as a finished product. Finished products are difficult to achieve in football. If you talk about us at an advanced stage of the process, we’ve been working for three months. If you exclude pre-season and the international break, we’ve been working for a month and a half. Far from being a finished product, we’re at the very beginning of the process. Our manager is still getting to know the team, analysing things and establishing his approach. The players are still getting to know me, too. I don’t think it’s fair to compare a team like ours with one that has been together for longer.” While recognizing Lamine Yamal’s talent, the Portuguese coach assured his team would not change its approach too much to contain him: “Lamine? They’re all very good players. It’s the same at Madrid. I haven’t been able to find a player who isn’t very good. He’s a great player. Respecting an opponent is one thing; changing your plans or forgetting your own identity is another. We won’t do that, not for him or for any other high-quality opponent.” Mourinho also had some words of praise for Hansi Flick: “I don’t understand why I’m being asked questions about our opponents. He’s a great manager and is doing an excellent job. I can’t say anything more.” The Real Madrid coach once again recognized his opponents’ strength, but assured that playing at the Spotify Camp Nou is just like playing at any other away stadium: “It’s just like going to any other stadium. We’re talking about a team of great quality. Playing against a high-quality team is not the same as playing against a team of lesser quality.” Reacting to Fermin Lopez’s words, the Portuguese coach took another veiled shot at the refereeing: “Perhaps. There are other things that keep happening that we’re getting tired of.” Mourinho also assured that him supporting a beard has nothing to do with superstitions: “I’m not superstitious at all. Do I look terrible with a beard? Should I change it? (Laughs.) I’m one of the few people in football without any superstitions.” The Real Madrid coach was not too ready to reveal his starting lineup: “Yes, but I can’t answer that question. I won’t discuss plans or tactical structures. You’re clever, but I’m not stupid. (Laughs.)“ Jose Mourinho took his Real Madrid team into some memorable matches against Barcelona during his first stint on the Merengue bench. Hopefully, he will be able to turn the recent trend in El Clasicos and get his side a win in this crucial game on Sunday, and make this upcoming match another memorable meeting between the two sides.

item.title: Tarik Skubal is rumored, but is he right for Padres?
item.description: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 06: Tarik Skubal (29) of the Los Angeles Dodgers watches from the dugout the NLDS game 3 between the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Atlanta Braves on October 6, 2026 at Truist Park in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Tarik Skubal is the top free agent on the market. On top of that he is a left-handed ace that should be the Opening Day starter for any team in the league not named the Los Angeles Dodgers, Atlanta Braves, Milwaukee Brewers or Pittsburgh Pirates… and even those teams would strongly consider putting Skubal on the mound in Game 1 of the 2027 season. The San Diego Padres have been rumored as a possible landing spot for the lefty in at least a few publications , and the argument for the move is that it would echo the commitment new owners Jose E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones made in press conferences and in their end-of-season letter to season ticket holders. The Padres are in need of pitching this offseason and a move to land Skubal would show the Padres fans and MLB the new owners mean what they say. The question all San Diego fans have to ask themselves is whether or not Skubal is worth the huge payday he is expected to get. Padres fans know all too well how volatile a pitcher can be. Joe Musgrove missed the majority of two seasons with an elbow injury, Nick Pivetta missed most of the 2026 season with an arm injury and Yu Darvish never touched the mound this season as a result of an arm injury. San Diego ace and likely soon-to-be free agent Michael King missed a chunk of the 2025 season because he “slept wrong” and injured a nerve in his shoulder/neck. Should the Padres want to spread their money around, whatever amount that might be, they may be better served. King is likely to opt-out of his contract and enter free agency. Reliever Adrian Morejon is a free agent and Ty France who many believe is the 2026 team MVP for the Padres is also a free agent. If Skubal wants $400 million-plus, it may be too rich for one player on a team that needs several players in the rotation and in the starting lineup. San Diego could have a rotation of Pivetta, if the Padres pick up his option, Musgrove and Randy Vasquez. Others who could make a push for the spot like JP Sears are also on the roster, but unlikely to find what is needed to be in the San Diego rotation to start the season. Musgrove is still an unknown in terms of what he can provide and Darvish COULD return, but he could also just as easily retire depending on how he feels once he gets back to throwing competitive pitches off the mound. This is an important offseason for the new ownership and as flashy as a Skubal signing might be, it may not be the most beneficial move for the team. Padres News: Walker Buhler gets his grade from Lincoln Zdunich of Gaslamp Ball after his first season in a Padres uniform. Baseball News: Milwaukee takes Game 1 of World Series with 3-2 win over Tampa Bay. Brewers

item.title: City slip to first Premier League loss of the season at Villa
item.description: City slip to first Premier League loss of the season at Villa City’s perfect start to the Premier League season was checked as the Blues went down to a 2-1 defeat away at Aston Villa. Enzo Maresca’s men had stepped out seeking to record a club record eighth successive league victory. However, a brace from Nicolas Jackson proved decisive, the Senegalese striker opening the scoring on six minutes and then striking again on the hour to restore the hosts’ lead shorty after Erling Haaland had headed City level. The Blues were largely dominant and carved out a host of opportunities with Villa keeper Zion Suzuki also making a series of fine saves. However, that pressure proved in vain as City went down to what was a fourth successive league loss at Villa Park. The game in brief City stepped out seeking to extend a perfect start to the league season, but it was Villa who flew out of the traps first, the hosts taking a sixth minute lead through danger man Jackson. Marc Guéhi took a heavy touch as City sought to build from the back and that allowed John McGinn the opportunity to put in Jackson as he ghosted into the Blues box. The Senegalese striker still had work to but cut inside Elliot Anderson before firing home past Gianluigi Donnarumma. It was a blow but only served to fire Maresca’s men up who suddenly began to dictate affairs in what was a high-octane, high-quality affair. Villa keeper Zion Suzuki needed to dive well to his right to deny Iliman Ndiaye after the winger cut in from the right before unleashing a superb goal bound drive on 14 minutes. The Japanese international then did even better on 21 minutes getting down early to smother a Rayan Cherki effort after some superb work from Doku on the left flank. City were knocking ever louder on the door and only the foot of the post denied Ndiaye - who was outstanding - after another jinking run and shot by the Senegalese. Villa were a potent threat on the break however and it required a superb tackle from skipper Rúben Dias to prevent Alysson striking potentially doubling the hosts lead on 39 minutes. Maresca opted to shake things up at the break, introducing Rico Lewis and Phil Foden in place of Guéhi and Cherki who were both on yellow cards. And the response was instant with City drawing level through Haaland just seven minutes after the restart. From a neatly worked free-kick, Ndiyae delivered a pinpoint cross and Haaland needed no second invitation to rise and head home his ninth league goal of the season. With our tails up it needed another fine save from Suzuki to keep Gvardiol out after the Croatian had latched onto a fine Doku ball. But, out of nowhere Villa hit back to regain the lead on the hour through that man Jackson. TEAMS ASTON VILLA XI: Suzuki, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Gomes (Madjo 82), Kamara, McGinn (C) (Buendia 66), Manzambi (Barkley 66), Alysson, Jackson (Goretzska 82) Subs: Bizot, Mings, Mbaye, Bogarde, Hemmings CITY XI: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Guéhi (Lewis 45), Gvardiol, Anderson, Fernández, Ndiaye (McAidoo 69), Cherki (Foden 45), Doku, Haaland Subs: Subs: Rulli, Kovačić, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Bouaddi, O’Reilly. item.title: COTA boss answers Max Verstappen's bump criticism: Turn 1 'not acceptable in my mind'
item.description: Circuit of the Americas owner Bobby Epstein has answered Max Verstappen 's claim that the bumps in Austin are "out of control". He insists the track is "in really good shape" with the sole exception of Turn 1, and he admits that problem has no quick fix. Prior to this weekend's US GP action, Verstappen slammed the "unacceptable" track surface at COTA after initially joking post-Singapore that he would need a "new spine" after the Austin weekend. "I was joking about that in the last race, but it's not really a joke to be honest. We mentioned this already for years, that it's actually getting a bit out of control," Verstappen said on Thursday. "I love this track, I love this place. It's one of the best layouts ever and it's one of the best venues, best city to be at. But for me the bumps are unacceptable. Over time they've been grinding a little bit here and there but it's just putting a plaster on the big problem." The 29-year-old later revealed spine damage he believes he has suffered as a consequence of bumpy F1 tracks, with an increasing concern the older he gets. Verstappen added: "It’s really not nice, and I think sometimes people don’t really understand that because I can tell you from the checks that I’ve done from my spine, the bottom end doesn’t look that great, the spine." Epstein admits Turn 1 dip has no easy fix Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Speaking to ESPN, COTA boss Epstein did not reject the criticism completely. He admitted that one spot at the bottom of Turn 1 falls short, but is confident the rest of the track is in "really good shape" having spoken to WEC drivers after their recent outing in Austin. "We don't feel good that there's a bump at the bottom of Turn 1," Epstein said. "We didn't know about it until this week. We would have fixed it. But the other things Max spoke about, all the bumps around the track, we've fixed them. The track is in really good shape. "I talked to some WEC drivers who said there's no problem. There's one bump at the beginning of [Turn] 1 that is not acceptable in my mind ... It's a dip, not a bump. If it were a bump, we'd sharpen it out, we'd take care of it tomorrow night, or overnight tonight, and that kind of stuff's happened before [at other circuits]. But when it's a dip it's a lot different, there's no easy fix." 'I had no problem with him saying what he said' Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Epstein also made it clear he did not take Verstappen's comments personally, and even joked that he had no doubt the Red Bull driver would agree with him once he had driven the track. "Max doesn't say I'm wrong a lot, but he's also right a lot, and he's usually very frank, and I appreciate that about him," Epstein added. "I had no problem with him saying what he said. I think he might be surprised in some areas that bumps he thought were here aren't any more." While not exactly scathing, Verstappen's initial assessment of Friday's practice action perhaps hasn't quite matched Epstein's

"I love this track, I love this place. It's one of the best layouts ever and it's one of the best venues, best city to be at. But for me the bumps are unacceptable. Over time they've been grinding a little bit here and there but it's just putting a plaster on the big problem." The 29-year-old later revealed spine damage he believes he has suffered as a consequence of bumpy F1 tracks, with an increasing concern the older he gets. Verstappen added: "It’s really not nice, and I think sometimes people don’t really understand that because I can tell you from the checks that I’ve done from my spine, the bottom end doesn’t look that great, the spine." Epstein admits Turn 1 dip has no easy fix Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Speaking to ESPN, COTA boss Epstein did not reject the criticism completely. He admitted that one spot at the bottom of Turn 1 falls short, but is confident the rest of the track is in "really good shape" having spoken to WEC drivers after their recent outing in Austin. "We don't feel good that there's a bump at the bottom of Turn 1," Epstein said. "We didn't know about it until this week. We would have fixed it. But the other things Max spoke about, all the bumps around the track, we've fixed them. The track is in really good shape. "I talked to some WEC drivers who said there's no problem. There's one bump at the beginning of [Turn] 1 that is not acceptable in my mind ... It's a dip, not a bump. If it were a bump, we'd sharpen it out, we'd take care of it tomorrow night, or overnight tonight, and that kind of stuff's happened before [at other circuits]. But when it's a dip it's a lot different, there's no easy fix." 'I had no problem with him saying what he said' Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Epstein also made it clear he did not take Verstappen's comments personally, and even joked that he had no doubt the Red Bull driver would agree with him once he had driven the track. "Max doesn't say I'm wrong a lot, but he's also right a lot, and he's usually very frank, and I appreciate that about him," Epstein added. "I had no problem with him saying what he said. I think he might be surprised in some areas that bumps he thought were here aren't any more." While not exactly scathing, Verstappen's initial assessment of Friday's practice action perhaps hasn't quite matched Epstein's expectations. The four-time world champion still flagged COTA's bumpy surface as a challenge during FP1 and FP2. In his brief review, Verstappen said: “It’s been a positive start to the weekend. This track is never easy when it comes to finding the right compromise between the low and high-speed corners." "The bumps make it even more difficult, so you’re trying to find a good balance in the car and get into a rhythm. That’s what we’ve been working on between FP1 and FP2. There’s still a bit more work to do to fine-tune that balance, but it wasn’t a bad day at all.”

item.title: Eye of the Tiger: Pivotal position matchups LSU vs. Auburn
item.description: ATHENS, GA - OCTOBER 17: Quarterback Byrum Brown #17 of the Auburn Tigers rushes the ball as linebacker Chris Cole #9 of the Georgia Bulldogs defends during the college football game between the Auburn Tigers and the Georgia Bulldogs on October 17, 2026, at Sanford Stadium in Athens, GA. Three years is too long to go without seeing these classic uniforms on the field together, so Saturday’s matchup is much welcomed. item.content:encoded: ATHENS, GA - OCTOBER 17: Quarterback Byrum Brown #17 of the Auburn Tigers rushes the ball as linebacker Chris Cole #9 of the Georgia Bulldogs defends during the college football game between the Auburn Tigers and the Georgia Bulldogs on October 17, 2026, at Sanford Stadium in Athens, GA. (Photo by Jeffrey Vest/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images For the first time since 2023, LSU and Auburn will square off for a Tiger vs Tiger matchup. This rivalry was a staple on the schedule year in and year out until the SEC abolished conference divisions. What was once a key battle for SEC West supremacy has now become an occasional matchup with Auburn not being one of LSU’s permanent opponents. It’s a shame, because this game seemed to always deliver. Both sides have had their moments, whether it be Flynn to Byrd, Cam “Superman” Newton, or Cole Tracy. Three years is too long to go without seeing these classic uniforms on the field together, so Saturday’s matchup is much welcomed. LSU heads in to Jordan-Hare as the #18 ranked team in the country with an overall record of 5-2, while 2-2 in the SEC. Auburn sits at 4-2 overall, while also 2-2 in the conference. They somehow just missed being ranked in the top-25, despite beating the #1 ranked Georgia Bulldogs on the road last week. That giant upset is very notable. Obviously it matters for Auburn’s resume, as they try to continue their ascent under first-year head coach, Alex Golesh, but the fallout from that emotional win could play a factor for LSU’s chances tomorrow. It’s never easy to come back down to Earth following a win as big as last week’s for Auburn. The emotion of the win spills over in to the following week of prep, no matter how hard you try to combat it. That doesn’t guarantee that it’ll be a benefit for LSU, but it’s certainly worth questioning whether Auburn is due for a hangover or is that the start of a hot streak. With both teams already having two losses, the loser of this game would seemingly be eliminated from playoff contention. It wouldn’t be impossible, but it would be highly unlikely to leave October with three losses and still have a reasonable chance. LSU is a touchdown favorite, which seems high. Yes, they have the better team on paper, but Lane Kiffin’s Tigers have yet to win a road game this year. If they want to finally jump that hurdle, it’ll start with winning some key matchups. LSU running game vs Auburn linebackers Dilin Jones is quietly the 4th leading rusher in the SEC. Folks in Baton Rouge may not be surprised by that, but with the occasional struggles to run the ball consistently on the road, he doesn’t get talked about as much nationally. His 4.4 yards per carry is top-tier, but it’s what he’s able to do after contact that has made him so special in this Kiffin/Weis offense. He has also consistently shown the ability to make defenders miss with his footwork and is constantly creating his own success. While he’s been hampered with his hamstring injury that has prevented him from running more, Sam Leavitt may be more willing to use his legs while on the road in a close game. We know how capable he is of being effective that way, so it will be interesting to watch just how healed he is. On the Auburn side, they’re playing with a massive hole in the middle of their defense. Former LSU Tiger Xavier Atkins was an All-American and extremely important to DJ Durkin’s defense. I say “was” because he is no longer with the team. Earlier in the week, he was dismissed after being suspended for the Georgia game. It’s unclear why, but what matters more for this game is that his absence against LSU puts Auburn in a tough spot. Bryce Deas will fill in for Atkins, but as a true sophomore who has only appeared in 10 games, so far, a matchup against Leavitt and Jones is a tall-task. He did show up and play well in his first start in Atkins’s place against the Bulldogs, recording the 2nd most tackles with 8. Thankfully for Auburn, they have a guy named Elijah Menendez, who is equally important to what Durkin does with his defense. He, too, is a true sophomore, but he played in 11 games in 2025 and has a lot of early experience. Menendez leads Auburn in tackles (59), tackles for loss (9), sacks (4), and pass breakups (5). He was all over the place against Georgia and is the top guy to keep an eye out for in this one. Look out for #9 to try and disrupt everything LSU wants to do on the ground. LSU defensive line vs Byrum Brown Each week, we could sit here and talk about how the defense’s front four is important against the opposing quarterback. Obviously, you may say. The difference this week is that LSU is going up against a 6’3, 235 pound quarterback who looks like a linebacker and runs with the aggression of a power running back. Despite his size and skill, he’s been sacked 23 times. Brown isn’t known as a thrower. He wants to run, so Blake Baker has his hands full. Think of the aforementioned Cam Newton or Tim Tebow. No, I’m not saying that he’s as talented as either one of those guys, especially considering that they’re two of the best college QBs of all time, but their style is what to keep in mind. If LSU’s front can’t find a way to get to Brown and disrupt him, he’s either going to have time to find an open receiver, which any SEC starting quarterback should be able to do with time, or he’ll find his spots to take off and punish you. He ran for 115 yards in the upset win over Georgia, despite only throwing for 150. LSU can’t let him do that and that starts with the front four. LSU secondary vs Auburn wide receivers The frustrations for Blake Baker and his soft zone coverage have been loud this season. Whether it be for the entire first half against Ole Miss, on the final drive of regulation against Kentucky, or even randomly against Mississippi St last week. Folks have not been happy about it. There’s merit to that frustration, too. Kiffin has acknowledged that it was his wish for the defense to defend Trinidad Chambliss like that, trying to avoid the big plays. Well, that resulted in methodical drives for the Rebel offense as their star QB took everything that the Tiger defense gave him. Same goes for Kenny Minchey, who easily drove the Wildcats down in to field goal range in Lexington. Despite neither of those games working out, could we see more of that strategy against Byrum Brown? I believe so, but it’s not for the same purpose. Brown doesn’t give coaches a ton of reason to fear having him beat you down field. He’s not very accurate, which is evident in both of Auburn’s losses. He finished with completion percentages of 57.1% and 57.7% against Florida and Tennessee, respectively. The difference between Chambliss/Minchey and Brown, though, is that Auburn’s signal-caller wants to run. Playing man defense against a QB that is looking to take off is a death sentence. The moment he sees defenders turn their back to him in coverage, he can take off. He’d gash the defense play after play. With a zone, Brown and everything else stays in front of each level of Baker’s defense. If he finds holes and makes throws, you tip the cap. But, the sort of approach that has frustrated fans earlier in the season may end up being the correct one for this matchup.

item.title: How to watch Texas vs Ole Miss tonight in Austin: TV channel, streaming info
item.description: Texas running back Hollywood Smothers (2) runs the ball during the game against Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Can Texas football recover tonight or will Saturday's game mark another low point in a rocky season? The Longhorns (4-2, 1-2 SEC) have lost two straight to unranked opponents, Oklahoma and Florida , 27-24. Now, No. 19 Texas has a tough test against a rolling Ole Miss squad. Texas football head coach Steve Sarkisian (left) and Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding (right). (Erick W. Rasco, Sports Illustrated Via Getty Images and Sarah Diggins) (Erick W. Rasco, Sarah Diggins) The Rebels are one of four one-loss teams remaining in the conference. They recorded a 31-3 win over Missouri, and that was after the Tigers had dominated Texas A&M and Florida by a combined score 72-23. The only blemish for Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1) on the season was a 52-28 loss to Florida. Questions have cropped up about Arch Manning as the starting quarterback for Texas, but Trinidad Chambliss is staunchly holding strong as the Rebels' QB1. Chambliss has 1,676 yards and 14 touchdowns and he is third favorite to win the Heisman Trophy behind Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith and Miami's Darian Mensah, according to DraftKings . A national audience will watch as UT tries to right the ship.
