item.title: Chiefs’ Josh Simmons Receives Blunt ‘Play Through Pain’ Advice From Franchise Legend
item.description: Josh Simmons is having an unlucky season with the Kansas City Chiefs , despite the team having much success. The franchise has won all five games it has played so far, and is yet to lose a game. They are showing serious signs of contending for the Super Bowl. However, Simmons has not been a part of the team’ success. He has missed the entire season so far due to injury issues. One former player believes that it should not be an excuse. Ex-Chiefs player tells Josh Simmons to play through pain Simmons was drafted back in 2025 as a first round pick, but has not had an easy time since then. After missing many weeks of action in his rookie season, the left tackle was placed on injured reserve on October 22, 2026, after his recovery from a bulging herniated disk in the lumbar spine plateaued. Jun 9, 2026; Kansas City, MO, USA; Kansas City Chiefs tackle Josh Simmons (71) speaks to media members during a short press conference after the Kansas City Chiefs mandatory mini-camp. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Previously, Chiefs legend and former left tackle Willie Roaf felt that the player should be playing, even if he is suffering from pain. Speaking on the Arrowhead Allies podcast , he said, “If it’s pain, then you got to be able to play through it. I mean, it’s the NFL. If we got to worry about you being in and out of the lineup, and your mental stability, it’s a different league with the mental part of this. These kids get to transfer in college; that’s not how the pros work.” He added, “These guys are used to a little more pampering going on. You’re going to have to grow up and understand that you’re a professional athlete. You have a responsibility to be ready to play every week.” However, the player’s issue has not improved significantly, and the team has preferred to let the player to recover through rehabilitation instead of surgery. One person has talked in detail on the situation. Update on Josh Simmons’ back issue According to Chiefs vice president of sports medicine and performance Rick Burkholder , Simmons first reported calf discomfort on August 17, 2026, during training camp in the same leg that required patellar tendon surgery in 2024 while at Ohio State. Team physicians correctly identified a lower-back issue rather than a leg or knee problem, an MRI confirmed a bulging herniated disk located higher in the spine than is typical for offensive linemen. This issue has complicated treatment. Burkholder said, “That disk problem was higher up than what we normally see in most of our offensive linemen, which complicated the case. The repeat MRI, a few weeks later, showed that the disk had improved, so no surgery was recommended. Josh worked his tail off. He worked diligently with my staff every day. However, we feel he has plateaued in the rehab process. He’s just not there yet.” He added, “I give a lot of credit to Josh, my physicians and my staff for navigating through this injury to the point where surgery is not recommended. He j

He’s just not there yet.” He added, “I give a lot of credit to Josh, my physicians and my staff for navigating through this injury to the point where surgery is not recommended. He just needs more time to return to full function.” Josh Simmons will miss at least the next four games and becomes eligible to return in Week 11. item.title: 68-point swing and a Tonga win - how England avoid World Cup exit
item.description: England bettered Samoa's margin of victory over a beleaguered France side [Getty Images] Sixty-eight. That is the magic number for England. For Brian McDermott's side to reach the semi-finals of the Rugby League World Cup, a specific series of events needs to happen next weekend. On the backfoot since being humbled 32-10 by Tonga in their opening game, England responded with a crushing 82-0 victory over France to keep their dreams alive. It means England need to beat co-hosts Papua New Guinea in their final group match in Wollongong next Friday – then hope Tonga beat Samoa, two days later in Sydney. If Samoa win, England will be eliminated because of their inferior head-to-head record against Tonga. They will also be knocked out if Tonga and Samoa draw. But if Tonga win, it comes down to points difference between England and Samoa. England's difference, after the Tonga loss and France win, is +64. Samoa, following hefty victories over the French and PNG, is +132 – which is 68 better than England. So, 68 is the number to remember. If England beat PNG by 68 points or more, then any Tongan win is good enough for McDermott's men. Less than 68, and they must hope Tonga are really inspired by Pacific rivalry to put one over their island neighbours. England hope the numbers go in their favour to avoid an unwanted first. In 16 previous Rugby League World Cups, staged in varying formats, neither England nor Great Britain have ever finished outside the top four. And every time the format has included semi-finals, they have got there. Group B-C: The remaining games Fri, 30 Oct: England v Papua New Guinea: Wollongong, 09:05 GMT Sun, 1 Nov: Lebanon v France: Parramatta, Sydney: 06:40 GMT Sun, 1 Nov: Tonga v Samoa: Parramatta, Sydney: 09:05 GMT 'I'm not sure what else we could have done' Tonga and Samoa are both above England in Group B-C with two wins from two [Getty Images] "What we have done today is enormous, given the context," McDermott told his post-match media conference in Perth. "Knowing we had to win big - and we have had candid conversations about that this week - we have done that without getting hot. Everything was measured and planned. "Whatever the results next week, we have to finish strong - if we go home next week, we will be disappointed, but I'm not sure what else we could have done." McDermott's final comments may allude to the controversial format of this men's World Cup, which features an unbalanced group stage that has not helped England's prospects. Pool A has four teams - Australia, New Zealand, Fiji and the Cook Islands - fighting for two semi-final places in a round-robin format. Simple enough. But Pools B and C are combined into one six-team league, from which only the top two will make the semi-finals. England, drawn in Pool B, play the three Pool C teams - Tonga, France and Papua New Guinea. item.content:encoded: England bettered Samoa's margin of victory over a beleaguered France side [Getty Images] Sixty-eight. That is the magic number for England. For Brian McDermott's side to reach the semi-finals of the Rugby League World Cup, a specific series of events needs to happen next weekend. On the backfoot since being humbled 32-10 by Tonga in their opening game, England responded with a crushing 82-0 victory over France to keep their dreams alive. It means England need to beat co-hosts Papua New Guinea in their final group match in Wollongong next Friday – then hope Tonga beat Samoa, two days later in Sydney. If Samoa win, England will be eliminated because of their inferior head-to-head record against Tonga. They will also be knocked out if Tonga and Samoa draw. But if Tonga win, it comes down to points difference between England and Samoa. England's difference, after the Tonga loss and France win, is +64. Samoa, following hefty victories over the French and PNG, is +132 – which is 68 better than England. So, 68 is the number to remember. If England beat PNG by 68 points or more, then any Tongan win is good enough for McDermott's men. Less than 68, and they must hope Tonga are really inspired by Pacific rivalry to put one over their island neighbours. England hope the numbers go in their favour to avoid an unwanted first. In 16 previous Rugby League World Cups, staged in varying formats, neither England nor Great Britain have ever finished outside the top four. And every time the format has included semi-finals, they have got there. Group B-C: The remaining games Fri, 30 Oct: England v Papua New Guinea: Wollongong, 09:05 GMT Sun, 1 Nov: Lebanon v France: Parramatta, Sydney: 06:40 GMT Sun, 1 Nov: Tonga v Samoa: Parramatta, Sydney: 09:05 GMT 'I'm not sure what else we could have done' Tonga and Samoa are both above England in Group B-C with two wins from two [Getty Images] "What we have done today is enormous, given the context," McDermott told his post-match media conference in Perth. "Knowing we had to win big - and we have had candid conversations about that this week - we have done that without getting hot. Everything was measured and planned. "Whatever the results next week, we have to finish strong - if we go home next week, we will be disappointed, but I'm not sure what else we could have done." McDermott's final comments may allude to the controversial format of this men's World Cup, which features an unbalanced group stage that has not helped England's prospects. Pool A has four teams - Australia, New Zealand, Fiji and the Cook Islands - fighting for two semi-final places in a round-robin format. Simple enough. But Pools B and C are combined into one six-team league, from which only the top two will make the semi-finals. England, drawn in Pool B, play the three Pool C teams - Tonga, France and Papua New Guinea. It means while England are competing with Samoa for a semi-final place, they will not actually play each other. It also means that while New Zealand lost their opening fixture against Australia, their path to the semis remains simple – win their final two group games. England too had to win their last two pool matches but also needed snookers. There is some reason behind the maddening format, introduced after France – who were supposed to host a 16-team men's World Cup last summer – pulled out because of money troubles. Australia stepped in with New Zealand and Papua New Guinea , with the number of teams involved shrunk from 16 to 10 to cut costs. This format also means every team plays three group games, there are no fallow weekends and the whole tournament can be done in a relatively tight five weeks. England thrash France to keep alive World Cup hopes Poor England suffer another Australia humiliation 'We have given ourselves half a chance' George Williams has captained England in their opening two matches in Perth [Getty Images] But it is unquestionably harder on sides in Groups B and C. The fact Australia and New Zealand are in Group A won't help the perception of the tournament being skewed towards the southern hemisphere giants. "We were the best we could be," England captain George Williams said of the France win. "The situation has been difficult, but we have given ourselves half a chance." It also leaves England fans with a nagging feeling their side are only producing their best when they are already halfway home. After a sluggish, disconnected showing against Tonga, England were slow starting against France before finding their mojo - no tries until the 23rd minute; by the final whistle they had run in 14. England's UK based players took nearly 48 hours to travel out to Perth. BBC Sport understands that the tournament organiser planned England's travel itinerary for the World Cup. The convoluted route featured a bus journey to London, then flights via Singapore and Sydney rather than straight to Perth, where they played their first two games. McDermott's side did not play a warm-up fixture and completed just two full training sessions before taking on Tonga. "We have been together for only five field sessions; we are building something here," said McDermott. "The tries we scored before half time were what we are chasing. "With a long build up, we could have achieved some special things." Ifs, buts and maybes. All England can do now is aim for 68 points, and hope.

item.title: Deshaun Watson Sends Strong Message on Jerry Jeudy Amid Browns Trade Speculation
item.description: The Cleveland Browns are sitting at 4-2 after Week 6 of the 2026 season, a position almost no one projected for them this early. That record includes a win over the Baltimore Ravens that improved them to 2-0 in the AFC North. Third wide receiver Jerry Jeudy haven’t been much effective but put on a solid performance against the Ravens which. With the current standings, despite the early shouts of trade possibilities, Cleveland Browns are unlikely to sell Jeudy. Cleveland Browns unlikely to trade Jerry Jeudy With the team winning, Cleveland has little incentive to become sellers. Jerry Jeudy has been the name most frequently linked to trade rumors, but dealing him now makes little sense for several reasons. Dec 2, 2024; Denver, Colorado, USA; Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy (3) before the game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Despite reduced overall production with 12 catches for 150 yards and no touchdowns so far, Jeudy has delivered in critical situations. Against the Ravens he posted four catches for 69 yards, including a 33-yard reception on the game-winning drive. He also made timely contributions in the win over the Steelers. Jeudy is currently the clear No. 3 wide receiver behind rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. Even as a higher-paid option in that role, he still provides reliable veteran production. The Browns do not urgently need the salary-cap space a trade would create. If Cleveland decides it no longer wants Jeudy long-term, it can revisit the market after the season. Moving him at the deadline while the team is winning and competitive would forfeit a useful piece for relatively little return. Deshaun Watson strongly backs Jerry Jeudy Quarterback Deshaun Watson reinforced the case for keeping Jeudy with a clear public endorsement as the team prepared for the Tennessee Titans. “He’s a true professional. He comes in each and every day, head up, smiling, encouraging everyone, encouraging himself, and he just puts the work in. He knew his opportunities were going to come, and it’s been there. He’s been able to take advantage of it. Everyone sees it. So that’s why you see the love and the happiness for the team because everyone sees the type of person he is off the field, but also the type of teammate and the work he puts in. Everyone loves to see the success that he’s having.” Deshaun Watson said . Jeudy’s role has shrunk significantly in 2026. Rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion have taken the top two wide-receiver spots, leaving Jeudy as the clear No. 3. Watson’s comments directly address that reduced role. The praise is consistent with earlier public support Watson offered after Jeudy delivered key plays in the Week 4 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. More NFL News: Patrick Mahomes’ Former Teammate Linked as Chiefs Reunion Candidate Chiefs’ Patrick Mahomes Leaves Every Other NFL Quarterback Behind in Latest Rankings Chiefs Face Offensive Line Concer

item.title: Arch Manning may already have a 2027 destination, per NFL insider’s source
item.description: NFL Network insider Tom Pelissero told The Bill Simmons Podcast this week that he put a simple question to one person who has known Arch Manning for a long time: where does the Texas quarterback land in 2027? The answer named a program woven into the Manning family’s history, and the same one that visits Austin on Saturday night. A 2027 college season is available to Manning because he redshirted in 2023, leaving him eligible through that year. His choice between the NFL Draft and one more college season has hung over Texas since the summer. “I texted one person who’s known Arch a long time, and I said, ‘Where do you see Arch in 2027?’ And his response was Ole Miss,” Pelissero said. Nov 1, 2025; Austin, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) warms up before a game against the Vanderbilt Commodores at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images The prediction is one unnamed person’s guess, relayed secondhand by a reporter whose beat is the NFL, about a decision that would come only after Texas’ season ends. It has traveled anyway because of what surrounds it, starting with Manning’s family tree. DEVELOPING: One person who has known Arch Manning for a long time predicts that he’ll transfer to Ole Miss for the 2027 season, per Tom Pelissero. “I texted one person who’s known Arch a long time, and I said, ‘Where do you see Arch in 2027?’ And his response was Ole Miss.” https://t.co/7hTSXGGwGI — Football Forever (@fballforeverhq) October 23, 2026 How strong are Manning’s ties to Ole Miss? His grandfather, Archie Manning, became the Rebels’ quarterback in the late 1960s, and Archie’s oldest and youngest sons, Cooper and Eli, also attended Ole Miss. Cooper is Arch’s father. Eli played four seasons in Oxford before going No. 1 in the 2004 NFL Draft. Arch took a recruiting visit to Oxford as a five-star prospect, when Lane Kiffin ran the program, before picking Texas. Kiffin has since left for LSU, and the Rebels are now led by Pete Golding, their former defensive coordinator, who was promoted to replace him. “I root for Ole Miss to win every other game probably besides that one,” Eli Manning said of Saturday’s matchup on Pardon My Take this month. At Texas, the 4-2 Longhorns lost to unranked Oklahoma and Florida in back-to-back weeks, with Manning committing a fourth-quarter turnover in both games. Steve Sarkisian said afterward that “everything” about the offense would be evaluated, and backup KJ Lacey was in line for more first-team reps in practice this week. Another loss could knock Texas out of the playoff picture entirely. Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) warms up before an NCAA football game against Florida in Gainesville, FL on Saturday, October 4, 2025. [Alan Youngblood/Gainesville Sun] Draft analyst Todd McShay has written that another college season looks like Manning’s best path for now, while saying he is more optimistic about Manning’s NFL future than the criticism online suggest

item.title: One of college football’s strangest nights resurfaced before LSU at Auburn
item.description: A clip from Jordan-Hare Stadium spread across social media again this week, ahead of Saturday’s noon ET kickoff between LSU and Auburn on that same field. The footage comes from Sept. 21, 1996, a night both fan bases still bring up whenever this series comes around. No. 21 LSU was visiting No. 13 Auburn that night in front of a sellout crowd of 85,214. During the first half, the Auburn Sports Arena next door, the wooden building everyone called the Barn, caught fire and burned to the ground as flames and black smoke rose beside the stadium. The game kept going, and the night has been remembered ever since as the night the Barn burned. Sep 23, 2023; College Station, Texas, USA; A detailed view of an Auburn Tigers helmet on the sideline of the game against the Texas A&M Aggies at Kyle Field. Mandatory Credit: Maria Lysaker-USA TODAY Sports The 2,500-seat arena opened in 1946 and was home to Auburn basketball until the program moved to Beard-Eaves Memorial Coliseum in 1969. It later housed women’s gymnastics and student activities . The blaze is blamed on a tailgater’s grill left too close to the wooden walls, and Auburn lore has long pinned that grill on LSU fans. “It looked like a major, major disaster was going on,” Terry Bowden, Auburn’s coach that night, said in 2016 . “We could have had a disaster on our hands,” former Auburn athletic director David Housel said . One of the craziest moments in sports history https://t.co/QJcaFdZvDG — Matt Wallace (@MattWallace888) October 23, 2026 How did LSU win a game it was outgained in by 122 yards? Auburn outgained LSU 363 yards to 241, but it turned the ball over four times and missed three field goals and an extra point. Starting quarterback Dameyune Craig was hurt and missed most of the fourth quarter, so backup Jon Cooley finished the game. Rusty Williams scored on a 7-yard run with 38 seconds left to pull Auburn within 17-15, and Auburn went for two to tie it. LSU’s Raion Hill intercepted Cooley’s pass and returned it the length of the field for two points of his own, making it 19-15. Hill had already returned a Cooley interception for a touchdown earlier in the night. Auburn recovered the onside kick that followed, and LSU’s Cedric Donaldson intercepted Cooley again to end it. Oct 7, 2023; Columbia, Missouri, USA; A general view of a LSU Tigers helmet against the Missouri Tigers during the first half at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-USA TODAY Sports LSU’s winning points came from its defense, on a play Auburn had called to tie the game, next door to a building that had burned down earlier that night. The fire is what keeps the clip circulating, but the finish was every bit as strange. “It’s one you never forget for weird reasons,” Bowden said . A parking deck next to Plainsman Park now stands where the Barn used to be. Thirty years later, Lane Kiffin’s LSU team arrives at Jordan-Hare as a 7-point favorite, and Auburn, 4-2 and 2-2 in the SEC, has already beaten a No

item.title: Nation’s leading receiver makes 2027 decision after breakout freshman season at Oregon State
item.description: The FBS leader in receiving yards and touchdown catches is a freshman who played defensive back for most of high school and drew one FBS scholarship offer as a receiver. On Friday, from Baltimore and live on CBS Sports HQ, he settled where he will play in 2027. That lone offer came from Oregon State, late on the opening day of the Early Signing Period, in a text from general manager Eron Hodges to his coach at St. Frances Academy, Messay Hailemariam. Teammates had already signed with Alabama and Auburn that day. Jesse Legree is staying with the program that sent the text. He re-signed with the Beavers for 2027, ending portal speculation that had started as other programs began planning next year’s rosters. Through seven games, Legree has 46 catches for 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns, and he is the only FBS wide receiver past 1,000 yards this season. He has gone over 100 yards and scored in every game, including an eight-catch, 240-yard night in a loss to Texas Tech, and he sits fifth on BetMGM’s Heisman board at 18-1. He has also been named Pac-12 Freshman of the Week seven straight times. Oct 3, 2026; Fort Collins, Colorado, USA; Oregon State Beavers wide receiver Jesse Legree (12) celebrates his touchdown against the Colorado State Rams with Aeryn Hampton in the first half at Sonny Lubick Field at Canvas Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Andrew Rydland-Imagn Images “I fell in love with the culture out there,” Legree told ESPN before the announcement. What did Oregon State’s new staff see that others missed? Legree switched from defensive back to receiver before his senior season, and Oregon State was the only FBS school to offer him at the position. He committed without seeing the campus, and asked about Oregon earlier this month, he joked that he barely knew it was a state at the time. First-year coach JaMarcus Shephard has said Legree was the first player he watched after taking the job. “The day I got the job, Eron called me and said, ‘Hey, watch this kid right now,'” Shephard said . “I didn’t know for sure how good of a receiver he was,” Shephard added. A freshman producing at this level would have been one of the most sought-after players in the portal, and Oregon State is rebuilding after its in-state rival left for the Big Ten. item.content:encoded: The FBS leader in receiving yards and touchdown catches is a freshman who played defensive back for most of high school and drew one FBS scholarship offer as a receiver. On Friday, from Baltimore and live on CBS Sports HQ, he settled where he will play in 2027. That lone offer came from Oregon State, late on the opening day of the Early Signing Period, in a text from general manager Eron Hodges to his coach at St. Frances Academy, Messay Hailemariam. Teammates had already signed with Alabama and Auburn that day. Jesse Legree is staying with the program that sent the text. He re-signed with the Beavers for 2027, ending portal speculation that had started as other programs began planning next year’s rosters. Through seven games, Legree has 46 catches for 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns, and he is the only FBS wide receiver past 1,000 yards this season. He has gone over 100 yards and scored in every game, including an eight-catch, 240-yard night in a loss to Texas Tech, and he sits fifth on BetMGM’s Heisman board at 18-1. He has also been named Pac-12 Freshman of the Week seven straight times. Oct 3, 2026; Fort Collins, Colorado, USA; Oregon State Beavers wide receiver Jesse Legree (12) celebrates his touchdown against the Colorado State Rams with Aeryn Hampton in the first half at Sonny Lubick Field at Canvas Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Andrew Rydland-Imagn Images “I fell in love with the culture out there,” Legree told ESPN before the announcement. What did Oregon State’s new staff see that others missed? Legree switched from defensive back to receiver before his senior season, and Oregon State was the only FBS school to offer him at the position. He committed without seeing the campus, and asked about Oregon earlier this month, he joked that he barely knew it was a state at the time. First-year coach JaMarcus Shephard has said Legree was the first player he watched after taking the job. “The day I got the job, Eron called me and said, ‘Hey, watch this kid right now,'” Shephard said . “I didn’t know for sure how good of a receiver he was,” Shephard added. A freshman producing at this level would have been one of the most sought-after players in the portal, and Oregon State is rebuilding after its in-state rival left for the Big Ten. The Beavers found a receiver the rest of FBS passed on, and in the first year of the Shephard and Hodges era, they kept him through the portal speculation. Oct 3, 2026; Fort Collins, Colorado, USA; Oregon State Beavers wide receiver Jesse Legree (12) runs for a touchdown against the Colorado State Rams in the first half at Sonny Lubick Field at Canvas Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Andrew Rydland-Imagn Images Oregon State is 5-2 and 3-0 in the Pac-12, riding a five-game winning streak into a bye before it faces Fresno State on Oct. 31. A Nov. 14 game against new Pac-12 member Boise State could shape which Group of Six team reaches the College Football Playoff. “We’ve built a great culture and it’s only going to get bigger from here. This is going to become the start of a national powerhouse,” Legree told ESPN. item.title: Who is supporting Gianni Infantino and how many votes will secure re-election as Fifa president?
item.description: Gianni Infantino is facing a battle to cling onto his Fifa presidency heading into next year’s election after his botched bid to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors resulted in a significant loss in support. England and Wales have been among the football associations to join European governing body Uefa in leading the charge for Infantino’s removal from power, formally withdrawing their endorsement of the Swiss-Italian for re-election in March 2027 . But as the dust has settled on his privatisation ploy, Infantino’s bid for a third term has strengthened. His allies have surfaced, with the likes of Mexico and Argentina joining Caf , the African football governing body, in reaffirming support for the under-fire president, and now the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has reversed its position and backed Infantino with AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa underlining that there is “a true understanding between us”. Infantino has now laughed in response to a question over whether he had considered resigning as president, declaring he retains the support of the “vast, vast majority” of world football. Infantino needs 106 votes from the 211 member associations to be re-elected as president . Here is every country and confederation to have expressed their opposition or support for Infantino: Who is opposing Infantino? Uefa (55 members) 🇪🇺 Uefa, the governing body for Europe, has staunchly opposed Infantino’s leadership. They threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions before Infantino’s eventual climbdown but has continued to assert that his position is untenable, even taking legal action against the Swiss-Italian. The body points to how there have not been “assurances” that attempts like the privatisation of the World Cup “to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again”. Uefa general secretary Theodore Theodoridis has written to his Fifa counterpart Mattias Grafstrom setting out a series of questions on behalf of European members of the Fifa Council, demanding documents covering a series of Infantino controversies. Fifa has until 2 November to answer these questions. Concacaf (41 members) 🌎 Concacaf, the Confederation for North America and the Caribbean, came out in opposition of Infantino after being left stunned at the lack of consultation during the Fifa sell-off plan, which they went on to reject. After the plan was aborted, the confederation said: “This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative.” Concacaf president Victor Montagliani was initially seen as a front-runner to challenge Infantino in next March’s election but he now looks set to pursue another term as Concacaf chief. item.content:encoded: Gianni Infantino is facing a battle to cling onto his Fifa presidency heading into next year’s election after his botched bid to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors resulted in a significant loss in support. England and Wales have been among the football associations to join European governing body Uefa in leading the charge for Infantino’s removal from power, formally withdrawing their endorsement of the Swiss-Italian for re-election in March 2027 . But as the dust has settled on his privatisation ploy, Infantino’s bid for a third term has strengthened. His allies have surfaced, with the likes of Mexico and Argentina joining Caf , the African football governing body, in reaffirming support for the under-fire president, and now the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has reversed its position and backed Infantino with AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa underlining that there is “a true understanding between us”. Infantino has now laughed in response to a question over whether he had considered resigning as president, declaring he retains the support of the “vast, vast majority” of world football. Infantino needs 106 votes from the 211 member associations to be re-elected as president . Here is every country and confederation to have expressed their opposition or support for Infantino: Who is opposing Infantino? Uefa (55 members) 🇪🇺 Uefa, the governing body for Europe, has staunchly opposed Infantino’s leadership. They threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions before Infantino’s eventual climbdown but has continued to assert that his position is untenable, even taking legal action against the Swiss-Italian. The body points to how there have not been “assurances” that attempts like the privatisation of the World Cup “to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again”. Uefa general secretary Theodore Theodoridis has written to his Fifa counterpart Mattias Grafstrom setting out a series of questions on behalf of European members of the Fifa Council, demanding documents covering a series of Infantino controversies. Fifa has until 2 November to answer these questions. Concacaf (41 members) 🌎 Concacaf, the Confederation for North America and the Caribbean, came out in opposition of Infantino after being left stunned at the lack of consultation during the Fifa sell-off plan, which they went on to reject. After the plan was aborted, the confederation said: “This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative.” Concacaf president Victor Montagliani was initially seen as a front-runner to challenge Infantino in next March’s election but he now looks set to pursue another term as Concacaf chief. England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 The English FA is one of many European member associations to send a letter to Fifa withdrawing its support for Infantino’s re-election in 2027. Infantino’s apology letter changed nothing for the FA, who was “deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance” surrounding his sell-off scheme. FA chief executive Mark Bullingham (left) next to Gianni Infantino (PA) Wales 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿 The Football Association of Wales was one of the first to send its letter withdrawing support for Infantino . “The ‌recent failures in good governance, processes, ‌leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgment ​have led us to a position ‌where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to ‌remain at the helm of world football,” a statement read. “Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.” Scotland 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 The SFA’s chief executive Ian Maxwell told the BBC that the governing body’s position has “been clear” since Uefa’s collective statement. He said: “We have aligned ourselves with the Uefa position and 55 nations are stronger than one voice. Their statement since then has talked about a lack of confidence in the Fifa leadership and the Scottish FA agree completely with that decision. The SFA will not be voting for Gianni Infantino come the re-election in early 2027.” Republic of Ireland 🇮🇪 The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) has followed in withdrawing its support for Infantino while backing Uefa’s stance. "Following an FAI board meeting, the decision was taken to rescind the letter of support that the Association supplied earlier this year," it confirmed. "It has since written to Fifa to explain its reasoning. The Association is grateful for the support that Fifa provides to Irish football, but recent events have raised significant concerns regarding governance, transparency and the lack of meaningful consultation.” Northern Ireland ☘️ The Northern Irish football association (IFA) has expressed “concerns” over Infantino’s leadership. "We take our responsibilities as a member association of both Uefa and Fifa seriously," said an IFA spokesperson. "We support the current Uefa position on the matter and will continue to engage constructively on issues relating to football governance. We are of course aware of the recent developments and wider concerns within the football community. We are considering these matters carefully and will continue to engage through the appropriate governance structures and channels.” Italy 🇮🇹 The Italian Football Federation (FIGC) initially delayed taking official action but it has now withdrawn its support for Infantino's candidacy in the next Fifa presidential election scheduled. "This decision is intended to clearly and transparently express the FIGC's position - in full agreement with Uefa and its president Aleksander Ceferin - regarding the recent initiatives promoted by the FIFA president concerning the governance and development of international competitions," FIGC said in a statement. France 🇫🇷 France withdrew their endorsement of Infantino in September and proposed to seek ways to transform how Fifa is run. "A project with such a significant impact on the future of football could not be envisaged without comprehensive information, in-depth consultation and a fully transparent decision-making process," FFF president Philippe Diallo said in a statement. "Fifa's governance does not live up to the standards that football represents." Belgium 🇧🇪 Belgium, who felt the brunt of another Infantino controversy at the World Cup over Folarin Balogun’s red card, have withdrawn their support for his re-election. citing Fifa’s failure to demonstrate “any transparency” under his leadership. Germany 🇩🇪 The German federation (DFB) already opted against endorsing Infantino earlier in the year so has not had to send a letter withdrawing support to take an opposing stance. “The DFB has not signed a letter of support for the re-election of Gianni Infantino," the governing body stated in July. "Further steps will be discussed in the DFB presidential board." Former Germany national team director Oliver Bierhoff further reiterated the nation’s loss of trust in Infantino: "We have to take care of football. It is already commercial but it is a property for all of football. The world views may be different but in the last weeks and months a lot happened so that we have no trust any more that it will be going in the right direction." Netherlands 🇳🇱 The Royal Dutch Football Association (KNVB) is among the many to have confirmed it has lost confidence in Infantino’s leadership. “The way this process has unfolded has resulted in a fundamental loss of confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino. The KNVB no longer has confidence in his leadership,” a statement read. Finland 🇫🇮 Finland kickstarted the process of formal withdrawals, with it being revealed that the Scandinavian member association was the first to send a letter officially withdrawing support for Infantino. Serbia 🇷🇸 The Football Association of Serbia then sent a similar letter to Fifa.

item.title: Jackson stars with two goals - player ratings for Aston Villa v Man City
item.description: Nicolas Jackson scored twice for Aston Villa [Getty Images] Nicolas Jackson scored twice as Aston Villa ended Manchester City's 100% winning start to the Premier League season. Here's how I rated the players and how you rated the players. What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean? Aston Villa Zion Suzuki: Good in the air, decent distribution and made three important stops to deny Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Josko Gvardiol with a brilliant, fingertip save. 7 Matty Cash: Battled all game with Jeremy Doku and though he was booked for a push on the Belgian, he managed more tackles than any other player. 7 Victor Lindelof: Threw his body at everything that came his way but outmuscled for Haaland's goal. 6 Pau Torres: Calming presence at the back without being too ruffled. 6 Ian Maatsen: Could have scored early on but blazed a volley over. Vital header away to deny Erling Haaland's goalbound header late on. 6 John McGinn: Picked off Marc Guehi to lay on the opening goal and created more chances than anyone else on the pitch. 7 Boubacar Kamara: At the heart of everything good from the home side, sniffing out the danger. 7 Joao Gomes: Mucked in alongside Kamara by keeping the ball ticking and contributing three interceptions. 6 Alysson: The 20-year-old Brazilian impressed against Viking in the Champions League and showed why he was given a start again with another eye-catching performance. 7 Johan Manzambi: Switzerland international displayed sparks of his undoubted talent and could have had a penalty in the first half. 6 Nicolas Jackson: Brimming with confidence. Took the opening goal brilliantly, firing high into the roof of the net, before stroking in a second. 9 Subs: Ibrahim Mbaye (on 58, Alysson) Instant impact after coming on, providing a low cross for Jackson to finish. 7 Emiliano Buendia (on 66, Manzambi) 6 Ross Barkley (on 66, McGinn) 6 Brian Madjo (on 82, Jackson) 6 Leon Goretzka (on 82, Gomes) 6 Subs not used: Marco Bizot, Tyrone Mings, Lamare Bogarde, George Hemmings. Manchester City Gianluigi Donnarumma: Conceded an early corner after taking too long over a goal-kick, poor kicking often put team-mates in trouble and should have done better for the second goal. 5 Abdukodir Khusanov: Shaky at right-back before being moved into central defence for the second half. 6 Ruben Dias: Rattled by Jackson in the first half but made a good block to deny Alysson a certain goal. 5 Marc Guehi: Another shocker. Culpable for both of Ipswich's goals last weekend and made another poor error which led to Villa's opener. Booked for hauling down Jackson on the edge of the box before being taken off at half-time. 4 Josko Gvardiol: Given a difficult time by Alysson throughout but came close to scoring in the second half. 5 Elliot Anderson: Struggled to impose himself in the game and was shown a yellow card for a mis-timed challenge on Gomes. 6 Enzo Fernandez: Always available for the ball but lost the midfield battle. 6 Iliman Ndiaye: City's liveliest player. item.title: Aston Villa 2-1 Manchester City: Flawless Villans end City’s perfect start
item.description: Aston Villa 2-1 Manchester City: Flawless Villans end City’s perfect start Aston Villa brought Manchester City’s perfect start to the league season to an end this afternoon, with a superb performance that saw them run out 2-1 winners at Villa Park. Villa opened the scoring when John McGinn and Nicolas Jackson combined to capitalise on a defensive error from Marc Guéhi after five minutes. Erling Haaland levelled early in the second half when he rose highest to head home from close range. However, Jackson popped up again on the hour mark when his shot squeezed under Gianluigi Donnarumma, eventually earning Villa all three points. As it happened Aston Villa made four changes from their Champions League win over Viking on Wednesday, with the most notable being the introduction of Johan Manzambi, who has been in fine form lately. Meanwhile, Haaland’s return to the starting side for Manchester City was their headline change after recent injury doubts and a rest against AEK Athens on Tuesday night. The first flashpoint of the afternoon saw the hosts awarded a corner after Donnarumma took too long over a goal kick. However, Villa couldn’t make the set-piece count. Their opener came just moments later, though, when Jackson cut inside on his right foot before firing into the roof of the net to give the Villans an early lead. City’s first real chance of the day came in the 12th minute, when Iliman Ndiaye danced round two defenders before forcing a good save from Zion Suzuki. Jackson drove towards the City defence five minutes later in search of doubling his side’s lead, but he dragged his shot wide. Suzuki was called into action again shortly after, this time getting down quickly to deny Rayan Cherki’s sweeping effort. A clever ball in behind from McGinn forced Josko Gvardiol to concede a corner on the half-hour mark, but the delivery was punched away by Donnarumma. Ndiaye came close to an equaliser again minutes later, this time striking the post with his curling effort. The end-to-end action continued when Manzambi saw penalty appeals confidently waved away by Peter Bankes after clashing with Elliot Anderson in the box. Guéhi was shown the first yellow card of the afternoon shortly after for a clumsy foul on Jackson, who looked to burst through on goal. Manzambi took on the free-kick but fired well over the crossbar. Cherki was next in the referee’s notebook, following a tactical foul on Manzambi. Alysson drove into the City box looking to put his side two to the good, but he was thwarted by some excellent defending from Rúben Dias, meaning it remained 1-0 going into half-time. Cherki and Guéhi were both withdrawn at the break, replaced by Phil Foden and Rico Lewis. It took just seven second-half minutes for City to draw level, when Ndiaye’s pack-post delivery found Haaland, who inevitably guided his header into the bottom corner. However, Jackson popped up again on the hour mark when his shot squeezed under Gianluigi Donnarumma, eventually earning Villa all three points. As it happened Aston Villa made four changes from their Champions League win over Viking on Wednesday, with the most notable being the introduction of Johan Manzambi, who has been in fine form lately. The first flashpoint of the afternoon saw the hosts awarded a corner after Donnarumma took too long over a goal kick. However, Villa couldn’t make the set-piece count. Their opener came just moments later, though, when Jackson cut inside on his right foot before firing into the roof of the net to give the Villans an early lead. City’s first real chance of the day came in the 12th minute, when Iliman Ndiaye danced round two defenders before forcing a good save from Zion Suzuki. Jackson drove towards the City defence five minutes later in search of doubling his side’s lead, but he dragged his shot wide. Suzuki was called into action again shortly after, this time getting down quickly to deny Rayan Cherki’s sweeping effort. A clever ball in behind from McGinn forced Josko Gvardiol to concede a corner on the half-hour mark, but the delivery was punched away by Donnarumma. Ndiaye came close to an equaliser again minutes later, this time striking the post with his curling effort. The end-to-end action continued when Manzambi saw penalty appeals confidently waved away by Peter Bankes after clashing with Elliot Anderson in the box. Guéhi was shown the first yellow card of the afternoon shortly after for a clumsy foul on Jackson, who looked to burst through on goal. Manzambi took on the free-kick but fired well over the crossbar. Cherki was next in the referee’s notebook, following a tactical foul on Manzambi. Alysson drove into the City box looking to put his side two to the good, but he was thwarted by some excellent defending from Rúben Dias, meaning it remained 1-0 going into half-time. Cherki and Guéhi were both withdrawn at the break, replaced by Phil Foden and Rico Lewis. It took just seven second-half minutes for City to draw level, when Ndiaye’s pack-post delivery found Haaland, who inevitably guided his header into the bottom corner. Manzambi and Matty Cash were both shown yellow cards by Bankes following the goal, the first for delaying the restart and the latter for a foul in the middle of the park. Gvardiol almost gave City the lead seconds later, flying up the left flank and forcing a great save from Suzuki. Villa’s first change saw Ibrahim Mbaye replace Alysson, whose impact was felt immediately when he set up Jackson to put them ahead on the hour mark by squeezing his shot underneath Donnarumma. Enzo Ferández delivered a dangerous corner five minutes later, picking out Gvardiol at the far post, but the Croatian’s headed well wide. A double change followed for the hosts, with Manzambi and McGinn replaced by Emiliano Buendia and Ross Barkley. Suzuki was on hand again in the 68th minute to deny Gvardiol from close range, before Ryan McAidoo replaced Ndiaye on the right flank. Anderson was the fifth player in the book today, after losing possession and lunging into a reactionary tackle that he never looked likely to win. Villa’s final changes came with 10 minutes to play, as Jackson and Joao Gomes made way for Brian Madjo and Leon Goretzka. Madjo was booked for time-wasting shortly after. Haaland almost popped up with another equaliser in the final moments of the match, but he saw his header cleared off the line by Ian Maatsen. That proved to be the final chance for City, as their perfect start came to an end.

item.title: Josh Jacobs on Packers fans who view him differently: ‘I’m not trying to win nobody back’
item.description: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs said Wednesday that he is not trying to win back fans who see him differently after his May arrest. Dec 7, 2025; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) during the game against the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Jacobs spoke for the first time since the incident, which led to his no-contest plea to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property. He missed the first six games on the commissioner’s exempt list and returned to practice Wednesday. The NFL’s review under its personal conduct policy continues. Wisconsin Sports Heroics has followed the case and the league’s investigation since the summer. Josh Jacobs: “I’m not trying to win nobody back” Keeping the organization out of a negative light is Jacobs’ priority with the public. “When it comes to earning the respect for the fans, I mean, for me, it’s more of a thing of not trying to put this organization in a position where it looks negative in any type of way,” Jacobs said. “But at the end of the day, people are always going to have their opinion. People are going to believe what they believe.” “And it’s not really my job to try to explain or discount certain things. All I can try to do is control what I can control and move on from there,” Jacobs continued. “Honestly, I’m not trying to, me personally, I’m not trying to win nobody back. And that’s just me being all the way honest. Because at the end of the day, like I said, I know what happened, you know,” Jacobs added. Josh Jacobs says it “should have never even happened” Jacobs also said he feels bad about the situation and understands fans who are upset. “And if you feel some type of way, obviously I feel bad because it’s still a situation that occurred and it should have never even happened. So that’s something that I still will understand if people feel some type of way about it,” Jacobs said. “But like I said, all I can do is keep showing up and being who I am. Being, you know, a leader for this team, being a leader in this community. And that’s really all I can control,” Jacobs continued. He opened the availability with an apology. He said he is “remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation.” Josh Jacobs did not feel he had to earn back the locker room Jacobs was a Packers captain the previous two seasons. “No, I don’t think I had to earn respect back from the guys because I’m the same person every day. Like I said, at the end of the day, we’re human. We all make mistakes. It’s just different for me because I’m in the public eye,” Jacobs said. “But, you know, like I said, I let other people speak to my character and who I am and who I consistently have been,” Jacobs continued. The Packers never moved off him. Coach Matt LaFleur said Aug. 28 that he “fully anticipate[s] him being a member of our team.” On Wednesday, LaFleur called Jacobs “extremely remorseful.” Jacobs’ status for Sunday
item.content:encoded: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs said Wednesday that he is not trying to win back fans who see him differently after his May arrest. Dec 7, 2025; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) during the game against the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Jacobs spoke for the first time since the incident, which led to his no-contest plea to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property. He missed the first six games on the commissioner’s exempt list and returned to practice Wednesday. The NFL’s review under its personal conduct policy continues. Wisconsin Sports Heroics has followed the case and the league’s investigation since the summer. Josh Jacobs: “I’m not trying to win nobody back” Keeping the organization out of a negative light is Jacobs’ priority with the public. “When it comes to earning the respect for the fans, I mean, for me, it’s more of a thing of not trying to put this organization in a position where it looks negative in any type of way,” Jacobs said. “But at the end of the day, people are always going to have their opinion. People are going to believe what they believe.” “And it’s not really my job to try to explain or discount certain things. All I can try to do is control what I can control and move on from there,” Jacobs continued. “Honestly, I’m not trying to, me personally, I’m not trying to win nobody back. And that’s just me being all the way honest. Because at the end of the day, like I said, I know what happened, you know,” Jacobs added. Josh Jacobs says it “should have never even happened” Jacobs also said he feels bad about the situation and understands fans who are upset. “And if you feel some type of way, obviously I feel bad because it’s still a situation that occurred and it should have never even happened. So that’s something that I still will understand if people feel some type of way about it,” Jacobs said. “But like I said, all I can do is keep showing up and being who I am. Being, you know, a leader for this team, being a leader in this community. And that’s really all I can control,” Jacobs continued. He opened the availability with an apology. He said he is “remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation.” Josh Jacobs did not feel he had to earn back the locker room Jacobs was a Packers captain the previous two seasons. “No, I don’t think I had to earn respect back from the guys because I’m the same person every day. Like I said, at the end of the day, we’re human. We all make mistakes. It’s just different for me because I’m in the public eye,” Jacobs said. “But, you know, like I said, I let other people speak to my character and who I am and who I consistently have been,” Jacobs continued. The Packers never moved off him. Coach Matt LaFleur said Aug. 28 that he “fully anticipate[s] him being a member of our team.” On Wednesday, LaFleur called Jacobs “extremely remorseful.” Jacobs’ status for Sunday at the Detroit Lions has not been set. Kickoff is 3:25 p.m. CT on FOX. item.title: Zero points should change Mikal Bridges’ Knicks assignment
item.description: October 2026 preseason archive, not the Boston regular-season loss. Oct 15, 2026; New York, New York, USA; New York Knicks shooting guard Mikal Bridges (25) reacts during the first half against the Toronto Raptors at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Zero points in 21 minutes is hard to explain away, even two games into a season. Mikal Bridges missed all eight of his shots Friday, including five threes, as the Knicks lost 107-103 in Boston. He’s 2-for-16 from the field through two games. I wouldn’t bench him out of frustration, but I would change the start of his night. Give Bridges an early curl or handoff that asks him to attack, rather than simply waiting for his next available jumper to restore everything. That’s a proposed first action, not a demand for extra minutes regardless of the result. The Knicks already have someone earning the time Miles McBride scored 20 points in Boston, hitting six of eight three-point attempts and playing just over 30 minutes. Bridges played 21:53. The reserve produced, and the minutes reflected it. That’s an important distinction. Giving Bridges a more deliberate early touch doesn’t require taking McBride off the floor when he’s helping the team. The Knicks can try to get a starter going while still rewarding the guard who is actually making shots. October 2026 preseason archive, not the Boston regular-season loss. Oct 12, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves shooting guard Anthony Edwards (5) shoots the ball as New York Knicks shooting guard Mikal Bridges (25) defends during the first half at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Mike Brown said after the game that Bridges is getting the looks he needs and has to make them, NBA.com’s Brian Martin reported . I don’t disagree with the basic expectation. An open shot remains a useful shot even when the last one missed. But there is room between changing the entire offense for him and doing nothing different. An early moving catch can give him a decision to make before the possession becomes another test of whether his jumper has returned. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. Four assists are a reason to keep him involved Bridges also had four assists and one turnover against Boston. The empty scoring line didn’t come with a complete inability to move the ball. If a defender closes hard on that early catch, a useful pass can still come out of the action. None of that guarantees a better shooting night. Two games are a tiny sample, and the simplest explanation may still be that a capable shooter has missed shots he normally makes. Keeping the existing spacing and trusting that recovery is a reasonable alternative. I’d give him that early action Sunday, then use the quality of his possessions and McBride’s production to help decide who finishes. Bridges should get a chance to respond before Brown

item.title: 🚨 Manchester City's first defeat of the season, Jackson scores twice !
item.description: 🚨 Manchester City's first defeat of the season, Jackson scores twice ! When Manchester City lose, the whole Premier League smiles. For the first time since the guilty verdict over the 115 breaches, the Citizens have dropped points in the league. Aston Villa pulled off the perfect result at home (2-1). Enzo Maresca felt the wrath of the player he had sidelined during his time in charge of Chelsea: Nicolas Jackson scored twice (in the 6th and 60th minutes) to inflict City's first Premier League defeat of the season. Erling Haaland had equalised shortly after the break (52nd minute). Before this setback at Villa Park, the Citizens had a perfect record: seven wins from seven matches. This defeat on Matchday 8 could allow Arsenal, who face Everton late this afternoon, to move level on points at the top of the table. item.title: Leaders Man City stunned by Aston Villa in first Premier League defeat
item.description: Manchester City dropped their first points of the Premier League season as Nicolas Jackson scored twice for impressive Aston Villa in a 2-1 win at Villa Park. City had won their first seven games of the campaign but Enzo Maresca suffered his first league defeat at the hands of Unai Emery ’s new-look side. Arsenal can go level on points with Manchester CIty if they beat Everton later this afternoon (Getty) Jackson, signed from Chelsea as part of the club’s drastic rebuild this summer, has now scored four goals in his last four appearances for Villa in the Premier League. The Senegal international opened the scoring after just six minutes as he punished an error from Marc Guehi before firing into the roof of Gianluigi Donnarumma ’s net. Maresca made a double-change at the break as he replaced Guehi and Rayan Cherki for Rico Lewis and Phil Foden, who was benched despite scoring a Champions League hat-trick in midweek. Erling Haaland scored for the seventh Premier League game in a row as he headed in Iliman Ndiaye’s cross to give City hope following the restart, before Jackson struck again. Aston Villa's Nicolas Jackson celebrates scoring their side's second goal of the game (PA) Erling Haaland scored in the seventh Premier League game in a row shortly after half-time (PA) The forward smashed in a shot from a low cross from Villa substitute Ibrahim Mbaye that squirmed under the body of the City goalkeeper Donnarumma. Villa failed to win any of their first four games of the Premier League season but Emery’s team have since won three out of their last four league games. Unai Emery’s team have now won seven of their last eight games after a slow start to the season (Reuters) Enzo Maresa’s side dropped points for the first time in the Premier League this campaign (Getty) City remain top but champions Arsenal could go level on points with them after eight games this season should they beat Everton at the Emirates this afternoon. City were playing in their second Premier League away game since the club were found guilty of almost all of the Premier League’s charges relating to breaches of financial rules last month. The club have appealed the ruling of the independent commission but they faced another hostile atmosphere at Villa Park and chants of “cheating b------s” throughout the match. More follows

item.title: Victor volleyball player reaches rare milestone of 2,000 assists
item.description: VICTOR – Setters are to volleyball what quarterbacks are to football. Namely, they run a team’s offense. Few weapons boost a team more than a quality setter. Victor enjoys one of Section V’s finest. Sophia Heltemes recently surpassed 2,000 career assists at Victor. Just a junior, she’s the catalyst behind one of the area’s top offenses. “(Heltemes) dictates where players go before serves and reads defenses,” Victor coach Matt Glover said. “She knows what our kids’ strengths are and tells them where to swing on the court. She is literally touching every ball on every set before it crosses the net.” More to come Heltemes first played varsity volleyball as an eighth grader, affording her experience she still carries today. It also gave her a head start toward career milestones compared with players who don’t reach varsity until later in high school. “(Setters) need to make a lot of decisions,” Heltemes said. “My teammates make it easy because they’re very reliable. I can always count on them to put a ball down.” Heltemes hopes to play college volleyball. She’s thankful for the talented attackers who have, and who still do, finish the plays she orchestrates. “I try to focus on our side and see who’s hot,” Heltemes said. “All of my teammates are really good at communication so that makes it really easy to run the offense.” Heltemes and the Blue Devils will soon begin pursuit of Section V glory in Class AA. “This is (Heltemes’) time to shine,” Glover said. “She is a fantastic player and someone to look out for. She’s going to make our team go a long way in sectionals.” Jeff Uveino joined the USA Today Network in 2023 and began covering Rochester-area high school sports in 2026. He is a graduate of St. Bonaventure University's Jandoli School of Communication and native of Perry. Contact him at juveino@usatodayco.com . Follow him on X @realjuveino and on Instagram @jeffusports. This article originally appeared on Rochester Democrat and Chronicle: Victor volleyball player reaches rare milestone of 2,000 assists

item.title: Bayern Munich star Manuel Neuer at doctor, status uncertain for SC Freiburg
item.description: (Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich may have another unexpected challenge to deal with ahead of Sunday’s Bundesliga clash against SC Freiburg, with Manuel Neuer’s availability now in serious doubt. According to Bild (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), Neuer missed today’s final training session at Säbener Straße ahead of the Freiburg match and was instead at the doctor’s office. While the exact nature of the issue has not been confirmed, his absence from the final session is hardly an encouraging sign with kickoff fast approaching. As things stand, Jonas Urbig is likely to start in goal for Bayern Munich tomorrow. The 23-year-old has long been viewed as Neuer’s long-term successor, and opportunities like this are precisely why Bayern Munich invested in his development. However, stepping in for the captain against a dangerous Freiburg side is no small assignment, particularly with Bayern coming off a demanding stretch of fixtures. The situation is made even more concerning by Vincent Kompany’s own health issues. Th e Bayern Munich head coach reportedly collapsed at Säbener Straße on Friday and was taken to the hospital for medical attenti on. The club has yet to provide a comprehensive public update on his condition, leaving uncertainty surrounding his availability for Sunday’s match. With bo th Neuer and Kompany dealing with health concerns, Bayern Munich could face SC Freiburg without two of their most important figures. An official update on Neuer’s condition will be crucial, but Bayern Munich may have to prepare for life without their captain once again. If Neuer cannot go, the gloves are likely Urbig’s to lose. item.title: Jeremiah Smith’s Heisman Case Gets Boost From Past Receiver Success After Julian Sayin Injury
item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes ‘ head coach Ryan Day has confirmed that their starting quarterback Julian Sayin will be out of for indefinite time period which ends his season only after 7 games. This might be big loss for the Buckeyes but is it going to stand in the way of wide receiver Jeremiah Smith and the Heisman Trophy? History provides blueprints that says in favor of Smith. Jeremiah Smiths’ chances for Heisman Trophy gets stronger Julian Sayin’s injury introduces real uncertainty into Jeremiah Smith’s Heisman Trophy campaign, but it does not necessarily end it and in some scenarios it could even strengthen the case. Sayin threw for 2,007 yards and 19 touchdowns in those same seven games before he was injured. Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) makes a one-handed catch in front of UCLA Bruins defensive back Andre Jordan Jr. (2) during the NCAA football game at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Nov. 15, 2025. Through seven games of the 2026 season, Smith remains the clear favorite. He has 52 receptions for 984 yards and 12 touchdowns, averaging nearly 19 yards per catch. He leads the nation in several receiving categories and has been the most dominant player on a top-ranked Ohio State team. Losing the starting quarterback means that Smith would have to play without an experienced quarterback and that could elevate Smith’s narrative. Receivers who put up big numbers alongside a polished passer are impressive, but a receiver who continues producing or even carries the offense while elevating an unproven quarterback is something rarer and more persuasive to Heisman voters. Jeremia Smith can hope remembering that Tim Brown in 1987 won the Heisman Trophy facing almost the similar situation. History provides hope for Jeremiah Smith In 1987, Tim Brown won the Heisman at Notre Dame after the Irish lost their starting quarterback to injury and turned to a less experienced Tony Rice. Brown had already established himself as the best player on a strong team, and the quarterback change did not erase that perception. As long as Ohio State continues to win, the narrative around him should hold firm regardless of who is throwing the football. Smith’s ability to create after the catch and win contested balls further insulates him. Those traits do not disappear with a new quarterback. Even if his raw volume moderates slightly, the quality of his impact and the context of Ohio State’s success can more than compensate. The injury forces greater reliance on him, and that heightened responsibility, paired with continued team success, strengthens rather than weakens the case that he is the most outstanding player in the country. item.title: Lions vs. Packers Week 7 preview: Madden 27 simulation
item.description: Welcome to another Saturday before the Detroit Lions are in action again. It’s a big week for the Lions, as the open up their divisional play with a home game against the Green Bay Packers. With the NFC North continuing to accumulate wins and top the NFC playoff race, this is becoming a pretty dang important game. But instead of waiting until Sunday afternoon to see what happens, why not find out who will win on Saturday morning? That’s right, it’s time for another Madden Simulation, and we’re going to be streaming this one live on our YouTube and Twitch pages. Just how accurate have our simulations been? Check out our weekly results: Week 1 vs. Saints Actual score: 31-30 Lions (OT) Madden score: 27-17 Lions (click link to watch the simulation) Week 2 at Bills: Actual Score: 41-31 Bills Madden score: 31-23 Bills Week 3 vs. Jets: Actual score: 31-24 Lions Madden score: 21-14 Lions Week 4 vs. Panthers Actual score: 32-26 Panthers Madden score: 42-14 Lions Week 5 vs. Cardinals Actual score: 45-21 Lions Madden score: 20-17 Lions (OT) 4-1. Pretty darn good. If you haven’t yet watched one of our Madden 27 simulations, here’s how they work. I adjust the lineups as close to what I think they’ll be on Sunday based on the latest injury reports. Then, we’ll pick some silly uniforms for each team. Then I take my hands off the controller and let the computer control each team to see what happens. I don’t call plays. I don’t make substitutions. Everything is computer controlled. And as we watch the madness unfold, I’ll be narrating the game, answering your Detroit Lions questions, and having a good time. So if you want to join, here’s all the info you need to know. What: Lions vs. Packers, Week 7 simulation on Madden 27 Where: POD’s YouTube page | POD’s Twitch channel When: October 24, 2026 — 9:45 a.m. ET Live stream will be embedded below when we’re live: View Link

item.title: 3 reasons why Alabama will defeat Texas A&M, 1 why not
item.description: Alabama (5-2 overall, 3-2 SEC) is looking to get back on track and snap their two-game losing streak as they host Texas A&M (4-3, 1-3 SEC) in a must-win game Saturday afternoon for the Tide. Not sure anyone had these two teams having a combined five losses by the time they matched up coming into the season. Nevertheless, here we are. Last week was a very forgettable one for Alabama as they fell 26-10 to Tennessee in a game that arguably was not that close. However, Alabama has the talent to turn things around quickly. With that being said, here are three reasons why Alabama will beat Texas A&M and one reason they will not. Why: Defense forces turnovers An area where Alabama has an opportunity to make some plays defensively is by forcing turnovers, especially interceptions. In their three SEC losses this season, Texas A&M has turned it over two times each game. In total this season, Marcel Reed has thrown six interceptions in seven games. After being +5 in turnover margin in their first two games, Texas A&M is -3 in their five games since. In seven games against ranked teams dating back to the start of last season, the Aggies have committed 13 turnovers, with 11 of those being interceptions. This game is an opportunity for someone like Bray Hubbard to come up with a big takeaway. Why: Pass rush gets home Another area where A&M has struggled recently is allowing sacks. In their recent losses to Missouri and LSU, the two groups of Tigers combined for seven sacks in those two games. In their last three games against ranked teams dating back to the CFP first round last season, Texas A&M has allowed a whopping 14 sacks. This game is an opportunity for the likes of Yhonzae Pierre and Devan Thompkins to make an impact in the pass rush, although the pass rush will have to be disciplined to not allow Marcel Reed to get free with his legs. Why: Big day from Lotzeir Brooks While the Aggies defense has been solid overall this season, so far they have been allowing big days to the other team's lead receiver. A couple weeks ago against LSU, Jackson Harris went for six catches, 163 yards, and two touchdowns and Winston Watkins Jr. also had a big day with five catches for 107 yards for LSU. Then, the following week against Arkansas, Chris Marshall had seven catches for 76 yards and a touchdown against A&M. Two weeks ago against Missouri, Mizzou's Cayden Lee had seven catches for 94 yards and a touchdown for the Tigers. Overall, the Aggies' pass defense is strong, but there are plays to be made for the opposing team's top receivers. If healthy, this would have been a prime spot for Ryan Coleman-Williams to have a big day, but Lotzeir Brooks is plenty capable. Why Not: Texas A&M third down defense Texas A&M has one of the best third down defenses in the country. For the season, the Aggies defense ranks No. 11 nationally in third down defense allowing just a 29.8% conversion rate. They have been good in their biggest games too. item.title: Natalia Granada Reveals the Family Element That Sparked Interest in Racing as She Navigates First F1 Academy Season (Exclusive)
item.description: Natalia Granada Credit: Anni Graf - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty NEED TO KNOW Natalia Granada began karting with her twin brother after watching Formula 1 races with their parents in Spain The 18-year-old F1 Academy driver is ninth in her debut season after a fourth-place finish in Zandvoort Granada balances online school and racing by cooking and spending time with family and friends For Natalia Granada, racing has always been a family affair. As kids, she and her twin brother, Marc, would watch Formula 1 races with their parents at home. And with a go-karting track just six minutes from their house in La Garriga, Spain, the Granada twins’ introduction seemed inevitable. “My parents were both F1 fans since forever,” Granada, 18, tells PEOPLE. “And I remember this moment, when my brother one day asked my dad, ‘How did Fernando Alonso, a very known Spanish F1 driver, start? How did he get to Formula 1?’ And so we started investigating.” The Granada twins discovered Alonso first got into go-karting. “From there, we just figured out the closest track,” Granada laughs. “I went there and started driving, and from there just one thing led to the next, and here we are.” As one of 15 full-time drivers in the all-women’s F1 Academy racing series, Granada is one of the sport’s brightest up-and-comers. In the final stretch of her debut season, Granada sits in ninth place as the series arrives in the United States to finish the year with two events in Austin, Texas, and Las Vegas over the next month. “It’s been amazing,” Granada says. “It’s just been such a big opportunity to make the jump from go-karts to single-seaters. It’s such a big step in my career, such a big opportunity in every aspect racing-wise, visibility-wise, for my future. I just think it’s been one of the best platforms so far for me to keep developing in my racing and my career.” Natalia Granada Credit: Anni Graf - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty It hasn’t been easy, though. Granada and the other teenage drivers in the F1 Academy — who come from all over the world to race in the series — must learn to navigate the balance of school, family and a social life, all while trying to compete at the highest level in hopes of one day making it to the top Formula 1 level. “Online school has helped me a lot to balance everything around my tight schedule,” Granada says. Outside of class and honing her skills on the racecourse, Granada says she takes her pressure off by cooking and spending time with her family. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! “I love cooking,” Granada smiles, sharing her love for paella and sushi. “And I love being able to go back home and see my family and friends, just to try and balance everything as much as possible so I can feel good when I have to get in the car.” Granada has appeared calm and collected behind the wheel this season, her first with the two-year driving program. In the most recent stage in Zandv

It’s such a big step in my career, such a big opportunity in every aspect racing-wise, visibility-wise, for my future. I just think it’s been one of the best platforms so far for me to keep developing in my racing and my career.” Natalia Granada Credit: Anni Graf - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty It hasn’t been easy, though. Granada and the other teenage drivers in the F1 Academy — who come from all over the world to race in the series — must learn to navigate the balance of school, family and a social life, all while trying to compete at the highest level in hopes of one day making it to the top Formula 1 level. “Online school has helped me a lot to balance everything around my tight schedule,” Granada says. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! “I love cooking,” Granada smiles, sharing her love for paella and sushi. “And I love being able to go back home and see my family and friends, just to try and balance everything as much as possible so I can feel good when I have to get in the car.” Granada has appeared calm and collected behind the wheel this season, her first with the two-year driving program. In the most recent stage in Zandvoort, Netherlands, the Sephora-sponsored racer finished in fourth, just off the podium — an exemplary finish for a driver on the cusp of breaking through in her sport. Natalia Granada and her twin brother Marc Granada Credit: Natalia Granada/Instagram The Spanish driver credits her improvement on the track to her team, the Iron Dames — a Swiss-Italian women’s racing group that’s helped more than two dozen women enter the sport since 2019, including Katherine Legge, who competed in this year’s Indy 500. “They’ve been such a big help for me, especially at this very young age,” Granada says, with her hopes set on becoming the next Iron Dames member to graduate beyond the F1 Academy. “This year, I’m working more based on how I’m feeling and what I’ve learned over the past years, and I’m managing quite well,” Granada reflects. “We always say in racing, you want to be very prepared for what you’re racing now and be ready to make the next step.” Read the original article on People

item.title: Cowboys Owner Jerry Jones Faces Harsh Criticism From Six-Time Pro Bowler for Having ‘Nothing to Show’
item.description: Jerry Jones invested a lot in the last offseason, determined to see the Dallas Cowboys succeed this season. The results have not been satisfactory so far this season. The team only has two wins in six games, having lost the other four games. Ahead of the team’s next game against the Philadelphia Eagles, one former player has come out against Jones and blamed him for the poor start to the season. Former Cowboys player blames Jerry Jones Former six-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle and ESPN analyst Gerald McCoy sharply criticized Jones on First Take . Amid the team’s poor start this season, Jones said that the team would potentially add players before the trade deadline, and refused to let go of players. Oct 18, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones looks on prior to the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images McCoy dismissed the billionaire owner’s words, and attacked him for his repeated failures over the years. He said, “We don’t care. Jerry, listen, you’ve been doing this way longer than me. You have three Super Bowls. I have none. You got way more money than I have. You are in a position that I am not in. But you are the owner, controller, CEO, all those titles you have. It is at minimum your job to do whatever to make your team better.” He continued, “We don’t care that you saying this because that’s your job. I believe that 31 other teams are believing and doing the exact same thing you just said.” McCoy further added that the current Cowboys roster already has high quality players since 2020. He said, “You don’t have a personnel problem. You currently on your roster have 10 All-Pro or Pro Bowl players, 10. And there’s five teams that are at the top of the league since 2020 with all pro and pro bowl players. The Cowboys are one of them and you have nothing to show for it. So it is not the talent or the players.” McCoy was not the only one to go after Jones for the team’s recent performances. Former NFL player criticizes Jerry Jones Former NFL player Breiden Fehoko also recently attacked Jones and his son Stephen Jones, who serves as an EVP for the franchise. In an X post , he said, “Jerry and Stephen Jones don’t know a lick of football and think money buys everything. Yeah, it can buy a nice Highland Park home, Jerry, but not heart or guys who’ll knock a [expletive] head loose. The Jones family are all micromanagers from grandpa Jerry to his kids. Jerry only wants yes men who’ll say, ‘Yes, Daddy, you’re right and everything you say is gospel.” He further added, “These draft classes have stunk. They’ve maybe hit on six players since 2019. Jerry is an oil man; remember that. He’s a business guy before a football guy.” Jerry Jones will have to move on from the criticism and hope that his team has a good result against the Philadelphia Eagles.
